title: How to photograph the August 27 lunar eclipse with iPhone Live Photos
content:
The August 27 partial lunar eclipse will place 96.3% of the moon inside Earth's shadow, and an iPhone Live Photo can give photographers several chances to capture a sharp image. Here's how to do it.

iPhone 17 Pro cameras
The partial phase begins at 10:34 p.m. EDT and reaches its maximum at 12:13 a.m. EDT on August 28, according to NASA. Before 10:34 p.m., the moon will pass through Earth's lighter penumbra, producing only subtle shading.
Most of North and South America will see the eclipse, while parts of western Europe and western Africa will catch portions of it. Unlike a solar eclipse, it's safe to view and photograph without protective glasses or a filter.

title: Tim Cook Stepping Down as Apple CEO Next Week: 15 Years in Quotes
content:
Tim Cook will be stepping down as Apple's CEO in just five more days, with the company's hardware engineering chief John Ternus set to take over.


Below, we have surfaced some of Cook's notable quotes over his 15 years leading Apple.

I want you to be confident that Apple is not going to change. I cherish and celebrate Apple's unique principles and values. Steve built a company and culture that is unlike any other in the world and we are going to stay true to that - it is in our DNA. We are going to continue to make the best products in the world that delight our customers and make our employees incredibly proud of what they do.
May 2012, on Apple's secrecy:
We're going to double down on secrecy on products. I'm serious.
September 2012, in a public apology about the botched launch of Apple Maps:
At Apple, we strive to make world-class products that deliver the best experience possible to our customers. With the launch of our new Maps last week, we fell short on this commitment. We are extremely sorry for the frustration this has caused our customers and we are doing everything we can to make Maps better.
December 2012, when asked if it is true that he wakes up at 3:45 a.m. every morning:
Yes, every morning.
The thing about it is, when you love what you do, you don't really think of it as work. It's what you do. And that's the good fortune of where I find myself.
October 2014, in a public essay:
I'm proud to be gay, and I consider being gay among the greatest gifts God has given me.
March 2015, the month before the Apple Watch launched:
Apple Watch begins a new chapter in the way we relate to technology and we think our customers are going to love it. We can't wait for people to start wearing Apple Watch to easily access information that matters, to interact with the world, and to live a better day by being more aware of their daily activity than ever before.
October 2015, on privacy:
We see that privacy is a fundamental human right that people have.
June 2017, expressing his excitement about augmented reality:
I think it is profound. I am so excited about it, I just want to yell out and scream.
March 2018, on what he would do if he were Mark Zuckerberg, amid a Facebook privacy scandal:
I wouldn't be in this situation.
March 2020, in response to COVID-19:
There is no mistaking the challenge of this moment. The entire Apple family is indebted to the heroic first responders, doctors, nurses, researchers, public health experts and public servants globally who have given every ounce of their spirit to help the world meet this moment.
August 2022, on Apple's legacy:
I think that when we look back one day and ask, what's been Apple's greatest contribution, it will be in health.
September 2022, in response to a customer asking why the iPhone did not support RCS, when Android smartphones already did at the time:
Buy your mom an iPhone.
June 2023, in Apple's Vision Pro announcement:
Today marks the beginning of a new era for computing. Just as the Mac introduced us to personal computing, and iPhone introduced us to mobile computing, Apple Vision Pro introduces us to spatial computing. Built upon decades of Apple innovation, Vision Pro is years ahead and unlike anything created before — with a revolutionary new input system and thousands of groundbreaking innovations.
April 2026, upon announcing he is stepping down as CEO:
It has been the greatest privilege of my life to be the CEO of Apple and to have been trusted to lead such an extraordinary company. I love Apple with all of my being, and I am so grateful to have had the opportunity to work with a team of such ingenious, innovative, creative, and deeply caring people who have been unwavering in their dedication to enriching the lives of our customers and creating the best products and services in the world.
And a list of Cook quotes would not be complete without:
Good moooorning!
Cook will remain at Apple as executive chairman on the company's board of directors. In this role, Apple said he will "assist with certain aspects of the company, including engaging with policymakers around the world."

title: PSA: Don't use a free iPhone that just turns up at your home
content:
If you get an unexpected iPhone shipped to you using it is just giving hackers your bank accounts and passwords. Here's what to look for, who to tell about it, and how to deal with it.


The sealed iPhone that turned up at a Reddit user's house - image credit: Remarkable_Source_64 on Reddit.
Well, maybe you do have a secret admirer, we're not judging and you are looking very good today. But a surprise gift of an iPhone will seem to be too good to be true because it is.
It will have been sent to you, or someone in your life who has a big job, in the hope, and possibly the fair expectation, that you won't question your luck and instead will enjoy the phone. Then every single thing you do on that phone is harvested and sent to fraudsters.

title: 2025 vs. 2026 Mac Studio Buyer's Guide: All Upgrades Compared
content:
Apple this week announced a new Mac Studio with the M5 Max and M5 Ultra chips, discontinuing the M4 Max and M3 Ultra models that had been on sale since March 2025.


The machine's design is unchanged for a fifth consecutive year, with all of the upgrades being internal. The table below details everything that changed regardless of whether you choose a Max or an Ultra chip. The two tables that follow break down the differences within each tier.

What Changed Across Both Models

Here's everything that differs between the 2025 and 2026 ‌Mac Studio‌ irrespective of configuration:







‌Mac Studio‌ (2025)
‌Mac Studio‌ (2026)


Baseline SSD read and write speeds
Next-generation SSD architecture built on PCIe Gen 6, with up to twice the read and write speeds


Wi-Fi 6E (802.11ax)
Wi-Fi 7 (802.11be) via the Apple-designed N1 chip


Bluetooth 5.3
Bluetooth 6



Genlock over USB-C




iPhone 17 lineup. Apple also says the new machine is made with 35% recycled content overall, including 100% recycled aluminum in the enclosure and 100% recycled rare earth elements in all magnets.

Mac Studio M4 Max vs. M5 Max

Here's everything that differs between the M4 Max and M5 Max configurations:







‌Mac Studio‌ (M4 Max, 2025)
‌Mac Studio‌ (M5 Max, 2026)


M4 Max chip
M5 Max chip


14-core CPU, configurable to 16-core, with 12 performance cores and 4 efficiency cores
18-core CPU with 6 super cores and 12 performance cores


32-core GPU, configurable to 40-core
32-core GPU, configurable to 40-core, with Neural Accelerators built into every core and enhanced shader cores


Second-generation hardware-accelerated ray tracing
Third-generation hardware-accelerated ray tracing


Up to 546GB/s memory bandwidth
Up to 614GB/s memory bandwidth


36GB unified memory with the 32-core GPU, or 64GB with the 40-core GPU (128GB option withdrawn in May 2026)
36GB unified memory with the 32-core GPU, or 48GB, 64GB, or 128GB with the 40-core GPU


Weighs 6.1 pounds (2.74 kg)
Weighs 6.0 pounds (2.7 kg)


Now discontinued
Starts at $2,499




The most immediately useful change is at the entry level. The M4 Max started with a 14-core CPU and could be configured up to 16 cores, whereas the M5 Max has an 18-core CPU as standard with no CPU upgrade to buy. Apple has also changed its core architecture, dropping the performance and efficiency split in favor of 6 super cores and 12 performance cores.

Mac Studio M3 Ultra vs. M5 Ultra

The table below outlines every difference between the two Ultra configurations:







‌Mac Studio‌ (M3 Ultra, 2025)
‌Mac Studio‌ (M5 Ultra, 2026)


M3 Ultra chip
M5 Ultra chip


28-core CPU, configurable to 32-core, with 24 performance cores and 8 efficiency cores
30-core CPU, configurable to 36-core, with 12 super cores and 24 performance cores


60-core GPU, configurable to 80-core
64-core GPU, configurable to 80-core, with Neural Accelerators built into every core and enhanced shader cores


First-generation hardware-accelerated ray tracing
Third-generation hardware-accelerated ray tracing


Dynamic Caching
Second-generation Dynamic Caching


819GB/s memory bandwidth
1.2TB/s memory bandwidth


96GB, 256GB, or 512GB unified memory (512GB option withdrawn in March 2026 and the 256GB option withdrawn in May 2026)
96GB or 256GB unified memory, or 512GB with the 80-core GPU


Now discontinued
Starts at $5,499




Across both generations, the maximum GPU still contains 80 cores, the Neural Engine still contains 32 cores, display support and media engine is identical, storage still maxes out at 16TB, and maximum unified memory is still 512GB. The 1.2TB/s of bandwidth feeding that memory, which is 50% higher than before, and the Neural Accelerators for each GPU core, are among the key changes.

How Big Are the Upgrades?

Apple's own comparisons against the outgoing chips are heavily weighted toward AI and graphics. For the M5 Max against the M4 Max, Apple claims:


Up to 3.9x faster LLM prompt processing in LM Studio

Up to 3.5x faster text-to-image performance

Up to 3x faster Magic Mask performance in Blackmagic Design DaVinci Resolve Studio

Up to 1.9x faster basecalling for DNA sequencing in Oxford Nanopore MinKNOW

Up to 50% faster graphics performance



For the M5 Ultra against the M3 Ultra, Apple claims:


Up to 4.3x faster text-to-image performance

Up to 4x faster LLM prompt processing in LM Studio

Up to 3.3x faster CopyCat ML training performance in Foundry Nuke

Up to 1.8x faster graphics performance

Up to 1.7x faster scene rendering performance in Maxon Redshift

Up to 1.3x higher multithreaded CPU performance



On either chip, tasks that use matrix multiplication can run three to four times faster thanks to new Neural Accelerators in each GPU core.

Which to Choose?

Apple no longer sells the M4 Max or M3 Ultra models, which became relatively poor value for money by the end of their run. The M4 Max cost $2,499 with a 14-core CPU and up to 64GB of memory. For the same price, the M5 Max has an 18-core CPU, 614GB/s memory bandwidth, up to 128GB of memory, twice-fast storage, and Wi‑Fi 7. The M3 Ultra ended at $5,299 with a 96GB memory limit. For $200 more, the M5 Ultra brings back 256GB and 512GB options and adds 50% more memory bandwidth.

Current M4 Max and M3 Ultra owners generally do not need to upgrade after only 17 months. Launch buyers paid $1,999 or $3,999, so replacing their machine now costs 25–38% more for the same design, ports, Ultra core limits, storage limit, and Media Engine. The main exception is AI-heavy work. Local LLMs, on-device image or video generation, and demanding machine-learning tasks in applications like DaVinci Resolve or Nuke can benefit substantially from the new Neural Accelerators. The M5 Ultra's 1.2TB/s memory bandwidth can also improve large-model token generation.

M1 or M2 ‌Mac Studio‌ owners. Apple says the M5 Max can process prompts up to 10.7× faster than the M1 Max, while the M5 Ultra can train ML models up to 15.4× faster than the M1 Ultra. Older models also lack Thunderbolt 5, AV1 decoding, and the newer Media Engine. If you already skipped the 2025 refresh, this is a more meaningful step forward.

The 2025 models are mainly worth considering used or refurbished at a steep discount. Apple raised prices in June, so lightly discounted older stock is often too close in price to a new model. One notable exception is an M3 Ultra with 256GB or 512GB of memory, since those configurations were unavailable new for much of 2026 and M5 Ultra equivalents will not ship until later this year.

late October, with pricing expected to start above $10,000.

discontinued the Mac Pro in March, seemingly with no plans for a replacement. There is no higher end Mac to wait for and no internal expansion path beyond adding a second machine.

title: Built-in Genlock makes the Mac Studio a boon for professional video production
content:
Apple has added Genlock to the new Mac Studio and the M5 Pro Mac mini. If you already know what that does for you, you've already called your production manager to make a purchase.


Genlock means you can sync the footage from a whole array of iPhones - image credit: Apple.
It wasn't the most high-profile aspect of the newly updated Mac Studio, but Genlock will be the reason some users buy it. Genlock is a system for synchronizing footage from multiple cameras and saves potentially hours of manually aligning video and audio tracks.
Genlock has been used by broadcast television productions for decades, and it has been supported by Macs and PCs before. However, it required third-party external hardware that was expensive and complex to use.

title: Apple Event: Six New Products to Expect on September 9
content:
Apple has announced that it will be holding an event on Wednesday, September 9 at 10 a.m. Pacific Time, with the company widely expected to unveil the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, its first-ever foldable iPhone, and more.


Other products expected to be announced at the event include an Apple Watch Series 12 with a ceramic case option, an Apple Watch Ultra 4, AirPods 5 with and without active noise cancellation, and potentially more.

Here are the six products most likely to be unveiled at the event.

Most Likely


iPhone 18 Pro: A20 Pro chip, a smaller Dynamic Island, a simplified Camera Control button, a Dark Cherry color option, and more.

iPhone 18 Pro Max: The same features rumored for the iPhone 18 Pro, but the Pro Max model may be slightly thicker due to a larger battery and a variable aperture camera, which might be exclusive to the Pro Max model this year.

iPhone Ultra: A foldable iPhone Ultra with a 7.7-inch inner display and 5.3-inch outer display, two rear cameras, one front camera, a Touch ID power button instead of Face ID, and more. iOS 27 is expected to be tailored for the foldable iPhone, allowing for side-by-side apps and other iPad-like multitasking functionality.

Apple Watch Series 12: A faster S11 chip or newer, longer battery life, fitness tracking improvements, and a ceramic case option.

Apple Watch Ultra 4: A faster S11 chip or newer, fitness tracking improvements, and additional satellite features for the Apple Watch Ultra 3 and newer, such as Apple Maps via satellite and the ability to send and receive photos with Messages via satellite. Touch ID was initially rumored, but seemingly ruled out.
AirPods 5: Two new AirPods 5 models with and without active noise cancellation.

Other Possibilities


Many of the products below are more likely to be announced in October this year, but perhaps some of them will appear at the September event.

iPad mini: A19 Pro or A20 Pro chip, an OLED display, a vibration-based speaker system, and a water-resistant design.

iMac: M6 chip and new color options.

14-inch MacBook Pro: A new 14-inch MacBook Pro base model with an M6 chip.

MacBook Ultra: A major MacBook Pro redesign in late 2026 or early 2027, with M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, an OLED display, a touch screen, a Dynamic Island, and a thinner design. On this laptop, which will reportedly be named MacBook Ultra, macOS 27 is expected to offer a touch-friendly interface.

Apple TV: At least five new features, including an A17 Pro chip or newer, an increased 8GB of RAM for Apple Intelligence, Siri AI support, an Apple-designed N1 chip with Wi-Fi 7 support, and an updated Siri Remote.

HomePod mini: Newer chip with Siri AI support, improved sound quality, Apple's N1 chip with Wi-Fi 7 support, a second-generation Ultra Wideband chip, and potentially new color options like red.

Home Hub: An all-new smart home hub featuring Siri AI, a 6-inch to 7-inch square display, an A18 chip for Apple Intelligence, FaceTime, and more. There will a tabletop version with a speaker base and a wall-mounted version.

title: If you ordered an M4 Mac mini, you may be getting a free M6 upgrade
content:
Macworld





Apple surprised us all by announcing a new Mac mini this week with an M6 processor and a higher price tag than the comparable M4 model it replaces. But if you’re one of the lucky people who had ordered one ahead of the announcement, you might be in line for a free upgrade.
The M4 Mac mini had been backordered for months, so this new model will hopefully offer some relief. While it’s not available until September 22, Apple’s online ordering system still guarantees you’ll get it on that date, even with the highest memory and storage options. That’s about a month earlier than some of the longest estimates for the previous M4 model.
So naturally, anyone who had an M4 on backorder would want to upgrade to the new model. The good news is you don’t have to—Apple is already doing it for you.
Numerous accounts on social media have shared an email from Apple regarding their M4 Mac mini orders:
Thank you for your recent Mac order. We know you’re looking forward to receiving your purchase.
As you may know, Apple recently announced the new Mac mini. Since your order has yet to ship, we automatically upgraded you to the new Mac mini at no additional cost.
The “no additional cost” bit is important. With the M6 Mac mini, Apple has raised prices by $100, so these buyers are essentially getting a $100 discount on a new M6. Not only will the machine be much faster, but it’ll also be a better value.
It’s not clear how far Apple is going back to offer upgrades. The usual policy is to offer refunds within a 14-day period, but some purchases have been backordered for much longer. So if you have an M4 on backorder and haven’t heard from Apple, reach out to the store. They may have a surprise waiting for you.

title: iOS 27 finally lets you separately adjust the volume of ringtones, alarms, and alerts
content:
Macworld





It’s one of the more persistently annoying aspects of owning an iPhone, and one of those dumb little things where Apple was overzealous in making things simple and left us with a frustration that most Android users haven’t had to deal with for years: Independent volume controls for various kinds of system sounds.
Sure, you’ve been able to adjust the volume for media (videos or music) separately from system sounds for ages. But there’s been one “Ringtone and Alerts” volume setting that controls everything else. Turn it up so your phone rings loudly, your timers will blast your ears off, and your alarm going off on your bedside table will make you jump out of bed. Lower it, and you risk sleeping through a wake-up call.
Now, at long last, Apple is giving us the ability to set independent volumes for different sounds. iOS 27 splits these sounds into three groups: Ringtones, Alarms and Timers, and Alerts and System Sounds.

				
					

				
			In iOS 26 (left) you have one system volume. In iOS 27, Apple lets you split it into three, if you want.
Foundry




Controlling these volume settings independently is easy and optional. Here’s where you find it:
Open Settings
Tap Sound & Haptics
Tap Match Ringtone Volume under Alarms and Timers or Alerts and System Sounds, as desired.
This will make a volume slider appear. Sounds will play as you adjust it, so you can hear how long or soft it is.

				
					

				
			
Foundry




If you like the simplicity of fewer volumes to adjust, you can simply leave the “Match Ringtone volume” switched on. So iOS 27 gives you to option to independently adjust just the type of system sounds you want. 
Adjusting the volume with your volume buttons when listening to media or on a call will continue to adjust the volume of just media or calls, the same way iOS has worked for years.

title: 6 Mac mini and Mac Studio upgrades you may have missed
content:
Macworld





Apple just announced the new M6 / M5 Pro Mac mini and M5 Max/Ultra Mac Studio, both of which are shipping on September 22. On the surface, these look like just the same Macs we have today with faster processors inside. But there’s more to them if you dig a little deeper.
Apple promotes these machines with nonspecific performance incremental values: 4.3x faster AI performance, 2x faster graphics, 4.8x faster LLM prompt performance, and so on. All of those claims will have to wait until we can do real testing with real applications. But while the outside of the Macs hasn’t changed, there are a number of features and differences you may have glossed over. Here are some of the more interesting differences between these new Macs and their predecessors.
Faster storage: Both the new Mac minis and Mac Studios feature SSDs using the new PCIe Gen 6 standard, with speeds up to twice as fast. Storage performance is a bottleneck to overall system responsiveness more often than you think, so this should really make a difference.
Upgraded Ethernet: The Mac mini used to come with a standard gigabit Ethernet port; that has now been upgraded to a 2.5Gb port. The 10Gb port upgrade option is still there, while the Mac Studio still comes with a 10Gb port standard.
Better wireless: Both systems now feature Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, up from the Wi-Fi 6E and Bluetooth 5.3 of their predecessors.
Genlock support: Both the Mac mini and Mac Studio now support Genlock over USB-C, a special timing signal standard used to keep multi-camera video shoots in sync. It won’t matter to most users, but if you’re someone who uses it, it’ll cut down on extra equipment.
Dual Neural Engines: Apple’s chips have had a 16-core Neural Engine for some time now. But what’s better than one 16-core Neural Engine? Two! So the M6 has two 16-core Neural Engines. All the M5 chips still have one, including the M5 Ultra, though since it’s two M5 Max chips interconnected, it has a “32-core” Neural Engine, just like the M3 Ultra.
Higher refresh rates: In three- and four-monitor configurations, the M6 and M5 Pro Mac mini supports higher refresh rates. With three displays, the 4K resolution used to be capped at 60Hz; now it’s up to 165Hz for the two displays connected via Thunderbolt. The M5 Pro version can run three 4K displays at 165 Hz, while the M4 Pro was limited to 60Hz. For a single display, refresh rates are unchanged: 8K at 60Hz, 5K at 120Hz, or 4K at 240Hz.

Comment Corner
The percentage change in price of a product as impacted by rapidly rising prices in RAM and Storage isn’t purely depending on the discrete amount of each. 
Rather, it depends on the percentage of that product’s cost that is tied to those components. A product not having much RAM or Storage may mean you’ll see a smaller discrete change in cost but not a smaller percentage change. 
In the Apple TV’s case, what RAM and Storage it DOES have makes up a large portion of the product’s price already. 
It doesn’t have an expensive display or camera module to mask the cost of components like storage and RAM. As a result, if the RAM and Storage rises in cost, it has a much larger impact on the overall cost of the product. 
This is to say, it makes PERFECT sense why the Apple TV would see such a large percentage change in price with the increased price of RAM and storage. 
If there are products you’d EXPECT to see that level of change, it’s products like the Apple TV and the Mac Studio.

TL;DR: GoCable is an 8-function, 100W-capable USB-C and Lightning cable with data transfer, magnetic storage, an LED display, a cutter, bottle opener, and carabiner for $24.99.
Most charging cables accomplish one job and then tie themselves into knots at the bottom of a bag. GoCable takes a more ambitious approach, squeezing eight practical features into a 5.9-inch keyring accessory that’s currently $24.99 instead of $49.99.
Its headline feature is charging at up to 100W, making it suitable for compatible phones, laptops, cameras, drones, and other gadgets. It supports USB-C-to-USB-C connections and includes an Apple Lightning connector, while an LED display shows charging status in real time.
GoCable also supports high-speed data transfers, so it can move files as well as power devices. When the job is done, its magnetic wrap keeps the cable organized instead of letting it audition for a role as a pocket pretzel.
Then come the extras. A built-in carabiner attaches GoCable to a bag or belt, while a safe-proofed hidden cutter helps open packages without leaving an exposed blade. There’s even a bottle opener, because apparently this cable refuses to clock out after charging your laptop.
The important catch is that GoCable doesn’t produce power by itself. Reaching its maximum 100W output requires a compatible wall adapter or power bank, which isn’t included.
For travelers, creators, and anyone tired of carrying loose accessories, this compact tool earns its spot in an everyday carry kit.

title: How to make Mac Downloads & other Dock folders easier to use
content:

Downloads on the Mac Dock
Apple treats Dock items as aliases that point to the originals. Removing a Dock alias changes only the Dock, so putting it back doesn't recover, move, or duplicate any files.

Open Finder and choose Go, then Home, or press Shift-Command-H.
Drag Downloads to the Dock beside the Trash.
Control-click or right-click Downloads in the Dock.
Choose View Content As, then Fan.
Choose Sort By, then Date Added.

title: Apple's iPhone Event Tagline is Different in Every Country
content:
Apple today announced it will hold its annual iPhone-centric event on Wednesday, September 9 at 10 a.m. Pacific Time. In the U.S. and several other countries, Apple used "Surprise and Shine" as its tagline for the event, but in other countries, the tagline isn't a literal translation.


Here are the different taglines Apple is using on its regional websites.

 	
U.S., UK, NZ, Australia, Ireland, India, Canada - Surprise and Shine.

 	
Canada, French - Des surprises dans l'air, or surprises in the air.

 	
Brazil - Surpreendente e brilhante, or surprising and brilliant.

 	
Mexico and Latin America - Sorpresas listas para brillar, which means surprises ready to shine.

 	
Germany, Austria, Switzerland - Staunen und strahlen, or something like wonder/amazement and radiate/shine.

 	
Spain - Un rayo de wow, which means a ray of wow or a flash of wow.

 	
France, Belgium - Un jour nouveau. Bientôt. The French phrase is a little different, translating to a new day, soon.

 	
Italy - L'alba di nuove sorprese, or the dawn of new surprises.

 	
Denmark - Det bliver solstrålende, or something like it's going to be brilliant/sunny. Solstrålende merges two words that mean sunbeam and brilliant.

 	
Norway - Tid for gode overraskelser, time for good surprises.

 	
Sweden - Förväntan. Förundran. Anticipation and wonder.

 	
Finland - Uudenkoitto, which translates to a new dawn or a new beginning.

 	
Poland - Zdumienia i olśnienia, which is surprise and amazement, or astonishment and revelation.

 	
Hungary - Ragyogó meglepetés, radiant/brilliant surprise.

 	
Portugal - O despontar de surpresas brilhantes, which translates to the dawn of brilliant surprises. Despontar is a word used for daybreak or sunrise, though Apple's Translate app says the phrase means "the unfolding of brilliant surprises."

 	
Turkey - Işıltılı. Şaşırtıcı. Heyecanlı or dazzling/sparkling, surprising, exciting.

 	
The Netherlands - Surprise party. Apple left this one in English.

 	
Czechia - Čas těšení, or time of anticipation.

 	
UAE, Saudi Arabia - بدايات تسطع بالمفاجآت, which means beginnings that shine with surprises.

 	
China - 亮新篇，来耀眼, which roughly means a bright new chapter, prepare to be dazzled. The 篇 character can also mean page of a book, which is perhaps an interesting nod to a foldable device.

 	
Hong Kong - 耀目驚喜，亮起新一章, translates to a dazzling surprise, lighting up a new chapter. It uses a different character for chapter and more clearly says surprise.

 	
Taiwan - 驚喜耀現，開新篇, meaning something like a dazzling surprise opens a new chapter.

 	
South Korea - 깜짝 빛날 시간, which translates to something like time to shine with a surprise. 깜짝 is surprise, 빛날 is shine, and 시간 is time.  


The different taglines make it clear Apple lets its regional teams write their own content instead of using the same translation worldwide. Taiwan, Hong Kong, and China all use the chapter concept, which is absent from the rest of the world. Many of the European translations use a new beginning or a new dawn, along with the same shining or radiant word in the U.S. version. A new beginning is similar to a new chapter, so the Chinese taglines are probably using that context rather than a book-like chapter context, but there may also be an intentional dual meaning there.

For all of the translations to English, there are multiple interpretations because there are characters or words with multiple meanings in English, or phrases that don't translate, but most have the same general meaning as Surprise and Shine.

Some regional Apple pages haven't been updated with the event info yet, including Japan, Korea, Brazil, Mexico, Thailand, and Vietnam.

iPhone 18 Pro, the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max, and the first foldable iPhone at its September 9 event.

title: Astropad Launches Rock Paper Pencil 4.0 With New Graphite Apple Pencil Tip
content:
Astropad today launched Rock Paper Pencil 4.0, an updated version of its screen protector and Apple Pencil tip combo made for the iPad.



Rock Paper Pencil offers a paper-like writing experience on a tablet display by pairing a paper-textured screen protector with custom tips for the ‌Apple Pencil‌. The new version of the product comes with two ‌Apple Pencil‌ tips, one with a smooth ballpoint feel and one that mimics a soft graphite pencil. Two of each tip come in the kit for four total.

Astropad says the new graphite tip is meant to feel just like a 2B pencil with a "soft, toothy drag" that's ideal for sketching or shading. It even has the sound of a pencil on paper. The ballpoint tip is meant to feel like a smooth gel pen, and it's suited to writing and linework.

The reusable screen protector remains the same as before, and users can put it on when writing or drawing on the ‌iPad‌ and take it off for other activities like gaming. It uses Astropad's NanoCling technology to attach, and it leaves no residue on the ‌iPad‌'s display because it doesn't use adhesive. The paper-like feel of the screen protector comes from a microscopic texture that adds a small amount of friction to improve control. When not in use, the screen protector can be kept in an included protective storage sleeve.


Rock Paper Pencil is compatible with most iPads, with a list available on the website. The tips work with all ‌Apple Pencil‌ models, including the ‌Apple Pencil‌ Pro.

purchased from the Astropad website for $49.99. Astropad is also running a "Peel It Off" promo that offers $20 to people who switch to Rock Paper Pencil and share the removal of their old screen protector on social media.

title: Meta Agrees to Limit Teens' Time on Facebook and Instagram, Calls on TikTok and YouTube to Match
content:
Meta today said it will implement major changes to Facebook and Instagram's child safety features as part of a settlement agreement with almost all U.S. states.


Here's what will change for users under 18 on Instagram and Facebook if the agreement is approved.

 	
Time Limit - Teens will have a two-hour daily time limit on Facebook and Instagram, though it can be overridden by a parent. The two-hour total includes both apps.

 	
Night Mode - Users will be blocked from posting and viewing content between midnight and 6 a.m.

 	
School Mode - Notifications are muted between 8 a.m. and 3 p.m.

 	
Prompts - The apps will send prompts after every 15 minutes of continuous screen time. There will also be prompts when daily usage hits 60 minutes and 90 minutes.

 	
Feed Control - Teens can choose a non-algorithmic feed that does not include personalization through the Instagram and Facebook recommendation systems. Parents will be able to require this setting.

 	
Autoplay Control - Teens will be able to turn off autoplay. Parents can require this setting.

 	
Hidden Likes - Teens won't see the likes and reactions on a post by default.

 	
Filters - Cosmetic surgery and extreme makeup filters won't be accessible to teens.

 	
Age Assurance - ‌Meta‌ plans to strengthen tools it uses to catch accounts belonging to users under 13, as well as accounts used by teens aged 13 to 17 to make sure the accounts have "experiences designed for teens."

 	
Parental Controls - ‌Meta‌ will add new controls for parents, notifying them if a teen links a second account or interacts with suspicious accounts. Parents will also get periodic updates on teen usage.

 	
Direct Messages - Direct messages are exempt from Time Limit, Night Mode, and School Mode.


‌Meta‌ will also pay approximately $18 billion to states to fund online youth safety initiatives, which is far less than its 2025 net income of $60.5 billion. The payment will be spread over a 10-year period, and ‌Meta‌ is withholding $5.3 billion unless TikTok and YouTube implement similar measures. If they do, ‌Meta‌ says it will lower daily usage limits from two cumulative hours across both apps to one hour for each app and expand ‌Night Mode‌ to run from 10 p.m. to 7 a.m.

posted an open letter calling on TikTok and YouTube to implement the same measures. Teens with restrictions on Instagram and Facebook could instead just move over to TikTok and YouTube, and ‌Meta‌ likely doesn't want to be the only company losing out on revenue.

Reuters. The settlement came before ‌Meta‌ CEO Mark Zuckerberg was set to testify, but Florida declined to settle and will continue litigation. New Mexico was also uninvolved because it won its own case against ‌Meta‌ earlier this year.

title: Apple Wallet IDs: How to add your license (and where it actually works)
content:
Macworld





Apple added the capability to add digital state IDs or driver’s licenses to Apple Wallet years ago, with the very first supporting states announced back in 2021.  
It’s a standards-based approach (ISO 18013-5) that is meant to be more secure and private than physical identification, as well as finally closing one of the last loopholes that make people unable to leave the house without their wallet.
If your state doesn’t support driver’s licenses in Wallet (or you don’t have a driver’s license), but you have an active passport, you can now add a Digital ID to your Apple Wallet.
Updated August 26, 2026: Your Virginia Mobile ID can now be added to Apple Wallet.
Add your driver’s license or ID to Apple Wallet
Adding your driver’s license or ID to Apple Wallet is simple, just follow these steps:
Open Wallet
Tap the “Add” (+) button in the upper-right corner.
Tap Driver’s License or State ID and select your state.
Now follow the on-screen instructions: First you’ll be asked if you want to add your ID to just your iPhone or your Apple Watch as well if you have a paired Apple Watch. 
Next you will be asked to take photos of your current ID, likely the front and back. 
You will then need to take some matching images of yourself. The phone will direct you to be in a well-lit area with a plain dark background and put your head in the frame. Then you’ll turn your head or make facial expressions (closing your eyes, opening your mouth) as directed by your phone. This information will be used to help match your appearance with your photo on record with the state. Think of it like a human making sure you look like the photo on your ID.

				
					

				
			
Foundry




States that support Apple Wallet ID
This is the current status of which states support Apple Wallet ID and which may be coming soon.


States that support Apple Wallet IDStates that have announced future support

ArizonaConnecticut
ArkansasKentucky

GeorgiaUtah

Montana

Will the U.K. support Apple Wallet driver’s licenses?
The U.K. government has announced plans to launch a GOV.UK Wallet and App in which licenced drivers will be able to store a digital copy of their driver’s licence.
The new app is coming this summer and the ability to store digital drivers licences, later in 2025. The digital driver’s licence will be piloted later in 2025, with plans to offer a digital alternative, alongside paper or card credentials, by the end of 2027. More here: U.K. iPhone users will soon be able to store digital licenses and IDs.
Why add ID to Apple Wallet?
Your ID in Apple Wallet is more secure than carrying around a physical card that could be lost or could reveal personal information to someone you may not wish to have it.
Digital IDs in Apple Wallet do not display any personal information other than your name. If you tap the (i) button to get more info, and then tap Driver’s License Info, your iPhone requires a Face ID or Touch ID login to see things like your address, date of birth, height, eye color, ID number, and so on.
The transaction starts over NFC and negotiates a secure Bluetooth LE session—no barcodes. So, you never have to hand your phone over to a police officer, TSA agent, or anyone else, and even if you do, they can’t get your personal info without your authentication.
Using your digital ID works a lot like Apple Pay. You hold your iPhone near the reader (which may be another iPhone), and a screen will pop up saying exactly which information you’re going to share. Double-tap the side button to approve it, just like approving a payment.
Currently, police agencies do not accept digital IDs as driver’s licenses, so you’ll have to carry your physical card with you when you drive. Rather, the feature works at select TSA checkpoints (see a map here) and participating businesses or age-restricted venues. What’s more, apps that require age identification (like renting a car or ordering alcohol) can use the info stored in Wallet to provide proof of age.
What’s nice about digital IDs is that they can transfer only the information needed, and nothing more. A bouncer who wants to check ID at the entrance to a venue would have a reader that shows your ID photo and simply confirms if you’re over 21, for example—they wouldn’t get your actual date of birth, ID number, address, or any other info they don’t need. The same goes for apps that need age verification. With the Apple Wallet implementation, nothing is transferred without your authentication, so not only do you not have to hand your phone over to anyone else, it wouldn’t even help to do so.
Why can’t I add my driver’s license?
If you are in the U.S. it may be that your state doesn’t yet support the feature. 
If your State is in the list above and you can’t add your license it may be because of an Apple Server outage (check that here). If that’s not the issue then Apple recommends contacting your “issuing authority”. 
If you are outside the U.S. it’s bad news. The ability to add ID and driver’s licenses is likely unavailable where you are. It’s not for Apple to implement the feature, but rather a decision on a country level. The U.K. government has announced plans for a digital version of the Driving Licence and other countries are likely to do the same.

title: iOS 27: 13 Ways the Messages App is Smarter and Less Annoying
content:
The Messages app is arguably the most important app on the iPhone, and in iOS 27, Apple is adding some useful improvements. There are some quality-of-life fixes for longtime issues, and new AI features.

Subscribe to the MacRumors YouTube channel for more videos.

Contextual Suggestions

Messages uses Apple Intelligence to surface one-tap suggestions based on what's being discussed in a conversation. If someone you're talking to asks you to send a photo, Messages recognizes the request and suggests adding the relevant photos.


If someone invites you to an event, Messages offers to add it to your Calendar. If someone asks you to pick something up at the store, Messages will suggest adding it to your Reminders list or to the Notes app.

Genmoji you might want to generate based on the conversation.

Write With Siri

There's a systemwide Write with Siri feature that's available in the Messages app. ‌Siri‌ AI can compose entire messages for you, proofread your messages, or give you feedback.


There is a dedicated Write with ‌Siri‌ button above the keyboard where you can get to the new ‌Siri‌ tools.

Smart Reply suggestions also use your writing style so they sound more natural.

Siri AI

‌Siri‌ AI integrates with the Messages app. You can ask ‌Siri‌ to find images, videos, links, addresses, phone numbers, and more in the Messages app, plus ‌Siri‌ can draft message replies and act on info in the Messages app, like adding an event date to the Calendar app.

Drawing

You can use a new Drawing interface in the Messages app to send little sketches and notes. It's available when tapping on the "+" button next to the text bar in a conversation.


The drawing interface is the same as the Markup tool available in apps like Photos and Notes. There's a marker, a pen, a highlighter, and an eraser, plus options to use the tools in any color.

Accidental Recordings

The ‌iOS 27‌ Messages app includes an option to remove the audio button from the text bar. In the Messages section of the Settings app, you can navigate to Show in Text Field to set the right-side button to Record Audio, Start Dictation, or None.


Setting the option to none will prevent you from accidentally recording a voice message with an errant tap.

Tapbacks

Messages now consolidates notifications for Tapback responses, which is useful when you're in a group thread and tons of people are sending emojis.

Sending

When a message fails to send in ‌iOS 27‌, your iPhone will automatically retry sending it. In iOS 26, you get an alert if a message fails, but you have to manually tap to try to send it again.

The Messages app also supports continuous sending of photos, videos, and texts. If you're sending someone a photo and your connection is poor or you go offline, it automatically resumes sending when the connection is restored.

Syncing

Cross-device syncing is improved in ‌iOS 27‌, so conversations will sync more reliably across the iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, and Vision Pro. Fewer messages will fail to sync and display properly when you switch between devices.

Messages, read states, reactions, and attachments sync faster.

When you take a photo and then go to the Messages app to send it, you're more likely to see it right away. Apple says the iPhone is faster to add recent camera captures to Messages.

Search

Apple improved its search index across apps like Mail and Messages, so you're more likely to find what you're looking for.

You can also search for conversations in Messages using a phone number or a contact's nickname.

Offloaded Media

If you have photos or videos that have been offloaded to save storage space, you can still find them in the ‌iOS 27‌ Messages app when you search.

Thumbnails are also displayed for offloaded media instead of a placeholder image, so you know what's there.

RCS

In RCS message conversations with Android users, you can now long press on a message to send an inline reply. ‌iOS 27‌ also shows reaction emoji directly on images and videos, a feature that was not functioning in ‌iOS 26‌.

Genmoji

Apple revamped ‌Genmoji‌ creation in ‌iOS 27‌. There's an updated interface for describing an emoji that you want, with options to start from an existing emoji, choose an image from ‌Photos‌, or select a person.


After uploading an image or using a text phrase to create a ‌‌Genmoji‌‌, there's a new "Describe a change" interface for making updates to what you've already created. You can iterate on designs and change individual elements of a ‌‌Genmoji‌‌, tweaking colors and objects. Each change uses the old base instead of regenerating a new ‌‌Genmoji‌‌.

With a series of requests, it is possible to make a complicated, multi-element ‌‌Genmoji‌‌. Along with describing changes, you can add in additional emoji, and the interface makes suggestions on what to do next.

‌‌Genmoji‌‌ output is more consistent, and ‌‌Genmoji‌‌ look more like real emoji with a 3D, cartoonish style by default. There is now an option to change style, so if you don't want the cartoonish look, you can ask for something else like a drawing or a sketch.

Large Conversations

Large conversations load and scroll faster in ‌iOS 27‌, according to Apple.

Read More

More on all of the features in ‌iOS 27‌ can be found in our iOS 27 guide.

Following this morning's announcement of the iPhone event that will take place on September 9, Apple added an event placeholder to its YouTube channel.



Apple will stream the "Surprise and Shine" event on YouTube, on the Apple Events website, and in the Apple TV app wherever it is available.

YouTube users can click on the video placeholder and choose the "Notify me" option to get a notification when the livestream is up. Apple also added an event countdown.

If YouTube has your location information, the notification and countdown will be displayed in your local time, so it's a good way to double-check when you will need to tune in to watch the event.

Apple's event will start at 10 a.m. Pacific Time, which is 1 p.m. Eastern Time, 6 p.m. British Summer Time, 7 p.m. Central European Summer Time, and 10:30 p.m. India Standard Time, 1 a.m. China Standard Time (Thursday, September 10), 1 a.m. Australian Western Standard Time, 3 a.m. Australian Eastern Standard Time, and 5 a.m. in New Zealand Standard Time.

You're also able to add the event to your calendar using the Apple Events website.

MacRumorsLive X (formerly Twitter) account so you can follow along with the announcements.

title: These are the new iPhone 18 Pro colors Apple will unveil September 9
content:
Macworld





It’s iPhone leaks season again. On September 9, Apple is expected to unveil three new phones: the iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max, and a new foldable iPhone rumored to be called the iPhone Ultra. But as always, one of the most important questions for buyers will be: What colors will Apple release this time?
Like last year, Macworld has received information from a source familiar with Apple’s supply chain regarding the color options for the iPhone 18 lineup. We can now reveal an inside look at the colors Apple is planning to release in September, along with our own renders to show what to expect.
Dark Cherry is the hot new hue
Every year, Apple introduces a new signature color for the iPhone Pro models. With the iPhone 17 Pro, the color that stood out the most was the vibrant Cosmic Orange. What about this year’s models?
While other sources have previously reported on a “Dark Red” color, the information we’ve heard suggests that Apple has been working on a Dark Cherry option to serve as the headline new color for the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max. Previously, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman and other leakers had suggested that Apple has been experimenting with a shade of red for this year’s phones, but we can reveal the hue will be much closer to wine than fruit punch.
While Dark Cherry color won’t be as bright and striking as Cosmic Orange in person, it will still be unique enough to distinguish it as the new iPhone 18 Pro. As always, Apple is expected to discontinue the current lineup of colors, including Cosmic Orange.

				
					

				
			
The iPhone 18 Pro could come in three all-new colors.

Foundry




Apple has also been reportedly experimenting with two other new color options for this year’s Pro lineup. One of them is Light Blue, which would resemble the current Mist Blue color of the base iPhone 17. The other color in development is a dark shade of gray. Finally, our source also reports on the existence of a silver variant of the iPhone 18 Pro, similar to the current generation.
Once again, our source notes that the colors are all in development, but since the iPhone 18 Pro hasn’t gone into mass production yet, Apple still has time to change them. Also, bear in mind that Apple doesn’t always offer four color options for the Pro models, so one of these hues could be dropped.
Last year, both Macworld and the reliable leaker Sonny Dickson reported that Apple had also considered launching the iPhone 17 Pro in black or steel gray. However, those color options never saw the light of day. 
Here are the Pantone color codes our says are being used internally by Apple:
Light Blue (Pantone 2121)
Dark Cherry (Pantone 6076)
Dark Gray (Pantone 426C)
Silver (Pantone 427C)
We used these codes to generate the image above. Of course, colors may look a bit different in real life due to the material and lighting conditions. Since this report was published, we’ve seen real-world evidence of these colors, specifically the Dark Cherry hue, so we’re confident it will be among the options when the phone arrives in September.
A very familiar design with minor changes
Macworld’s sources also had access to the CAD drawings of the new iPhones. These documents support the rumors that the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max will look very similar to their predecessors, with only minor changes.
Most notably, the renders show a smaller Dynamic Island on the screen, which has been rumored to be one of the changes for this year’s models. This means the display will have more screen space for content when the Dynamic Island isn’t showing Live Activities.

				
					

				
			
The Dynamic Island could be smaller on the iPhone 18 Pro.

Foundry




Another interesting change noted by our source is that, in one of the renders, the gap between the glass cutout on the back and the camera bump is a bit smaller. Our source was unable to verify whether this is an old render, or if Apple is moving forward with a design change.
Last year, a Weibo leaker known as Instant Digital reported that Apple would adopt a new process to minimize the color difference between the glass and the aluminum frame, so perhaps that change also involves reducing the gap between the glass and the camera bump at some point.
More neutral colors for the foldable iPhone
We’ve also received details about the color options for the rumored foldable iPhone. The device, which will reportedly look like an iPad mini when unfolded, won’t come in fun colors like the base iPhone and may have even fewer options than the iPhone Pro.
For the foldable iPhone, Apple has been working on a classic silver and white model, as well as an Indigo option similar to the iPhone 17 Pro’s Deep Blue.

				
					

				
			
The iPhone Fold will reportedly come in a dark Indigo option.

Foundry




The source also corroborates leaked CADs and renders showing the potential design of the foldable iPhone, which is expected to feature two rear cameras, a selfie camera on the outer display, and another selfie camera in the upper-left corner of the inner display. The schematics seen by our source reveal that the foldable iPhone will be just 4.7 millimeters thick when unfolded, making it significantly thinner than the 5.6mm iPhone Air.
The iPhone 18 Pro, 18 Pro Max, and the foldable iPhone are all expected to launch in September, while our sources also report that the foldable model will hit stores at a later date. The base model of the iPhone 18, the iPhone 18e, and a new Air have been rumored to arrive in the first half of 2027, which has also been confirmed by our source.

title: Surprise and Shine! Apple’s big iPhone event set for September 9
content:
Macworld





Apple has officially announced the date and time of its big September iPhone event: Wednesday, September 9, at 10 am PT. That’s a day later than its usual fall events because of the Labor Day holiday on Monday.
The event invitations went out with an image of an Apple logo shining brightly like a sun in the sky along with the tagline “Surprise and shine.” The event will be streamed on apple.com, on the Apple TV app, and on the Apple YouTube channel. We will of course have full coverage right here on Macworld including a liveblog.
Apple’s event invitations often contain some clue about what we expect them to announce, but it’s hard to imagine what this one could be referencing from the current rumors and leaks. There’s a bit of a “new day” angle with this being the first Apple Event under incoming CEO John Ternus, but we don’t expect anything related to super-bright displays or anything that would obviously relate to this motif. 
The prevailing color is blue, which could be a reference to one of the new iPhone 18 Pro colors, and the overall brightness could reference the new camera system. And we obviously want a surprise, but Apple tries to make every new event full of surprises.
Whatever it means, here’s what we expect Apple to announce:
iPhone 18 Pro / Max: With a similar design to the iPhone 17 Pro/Max, the next iteration of Pro phones will reportedly sport a new Dark Cherry color, a fast new A20 Pro chip, and a new main camera with a variable aperture. Learn more about the iPhone 18 Pro / Max.
iPhone Ultra: The first folding iPhone is expected to be called iPhone Ultra. According to rumors, it will have an unusually wide “passport” size when folded and include the A20 Pro, two cameras (wide and telephoto), and use a new Touch ID button instead of Face ID, but it’s the software features and capabilities that will really make or break the new product, of which we know very little. The price is expected to be high at $2,000 or more. Learn more about what we expect fromt the iPhone Ultra.
Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4: Apple always launches a new Apple Watch together with the new iPhones. This year that should be the Series 12, and potentially the Ultra 4. We don’t expect any big changes to either of these…there will be minor chip improvements for better performance, but the latest rumors say not to expect major design changes or big new features like blood glucose monitoring this year. Learn more about Apple Watch Series 12.
Other surprises could show up
Apple has multiple other products on the way soon that could make an appearance at this event, but aren’t necessarily expected. That includes a new Apple TV 4K and a new HomePod mini (both with chip updates that let them support the new Siri AI), as well as a totally new product: a smart home hub with a squarish 7-inch screen and a new operating system.
Apple just revealed new M6 Mac mini and M5 Mac Studio products that ship later in September. But there are other Macs in the works, including an entry-level M6 MacBook Pro, a touchscreen MacBook Pro with a totally new design, and an M6 iMac with new colors, but we expect those to be bundled at an event later in the fall.
Similarly, Apple is preparing AirPods with cameras. While AirPods are very often announced together with new iPhones, the rumor is that this model isn’t expected to ship until 2027. However, Apple could use this event to announce AirPods 5, according to a rumor this week from Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman.

title: Meta agrees to $18B settlement to end teen social hygiene lawsuit
content:
Meta has agreed to pay up to $18 billion and to make changes to Facebook and other online services, all to settle a federal lawsuit alleging teenagers are being harmed by social media.


Instagram, one of Meta's online social properties
Mark Zuckerberg's Meta has been dealing with a trial concerning the mental and social effects of social media for a while, but it's seemingly no longer a problem. The social giant has managed to hammer out a settlement with some functional concessions as well as a hefty fine.
The settlement is with 48 state attorneys general across the entire United States, including four jurisdictions, reports the Wall Street Journal. The exceptions are New Mexico, which won in a similar trial in the spring, and Florida, which didn't take part in the settlement.

title: Apple’s September iPhone event: Date, time, and what will launch
content:
Macworld





Apple has confirmed that it will hold an event on Wednesday September 9, starting at 1pm ET, 10am PT and 6pm BST. We expect that Apple will take the wraps off the new iPhone 18 Pro, new iPhone Ultra and new Apple Watches during the keynote.
Read on to find out everything you need to know about Apple’s iPhone launch event for 2026, including when the Apple Event will start where you are, and the new products Apple will launch. You will be able to watch the event below once it starts. We will also run a live blog.
When is Apple’s iPhone event?
Wednesday September 9
The 2026 iPhone event will take place on Wednesday 9 September, we had already predicted this date based on Apple’s tendency to hold the event around the second week of September so it is no surprise.
What time will the iPhone event start?






Apple Events usually start at 10 a.m. in California, and this one is no different. Here’s what that translates to in other countries and other locations:
U.S.: 10 a.m. (PDT), 11 a.m. (MDT), 12 p.m. (CDT), 1 p.m. (EDT)
U.K.: 6 p.m. (BST)
Europe: 7 p.m. (CEST) 8 p.m. (EEST)
Canada: 10 a.m. (PDT), 11 a.m. (MDT), 12 p.m. (CDT), 1 p.m. (EDT), 2 p.m. (ADT)
India: 10.30 p.m. (IST)
Hong Kong, Singapore and China: The following day at 1 a.m.
Australia: The following day at 1 a.m. (AWST), 2.30 a.m. (ACST), 3 a.m. (AEST)
New Zealand: The following day at 5 a.m. (NZST)
Apple’s September events are usually one to two hours long.
What will Apple launch at the September 2026 event?
Apple’s September events typically feature the launch of new iPhones, Apple Watches, and, sometimes, AirPods. Apple’s September 2026 event is shaping up to be one of its most significant in years, with a mix of expected updates and a major new product category: 
The Headliner: iPhone Ultra (Foldable) 
The biggest news is the long-rumored folding iPhone, expected to be called the iPhone Ultra . This marks Apple’s first major form-factor change in over a decade. According to reports, it will fold like a book, have a passport-like shape when closed, and feature a starting price of $2,000 or more . It’s expected to include two rear cameras (wide and ultrawide), a front-facing camera, and the return of Touch ID built into the side button. Read more here: iPhone Ultra rumors.
iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max
Alongside the Ultra, Apple is expected to launch the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max . These models are rumored to feature an upgraded A20 Pro processor, a new C2 modem (or Qualcomm in the U.S.), and a new “Dark Cherry” signature color . Camera improvements are also expected, including a variable aperture and new sensor technology, along with a potential boost to 24 megapixels for the front-facing camera. Read more here:  iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max rumors.
Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4
As is tradition, Apple will update its smartwatch lineup alongside the new iPhones. The Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 are expected to be announced . However, reports suggest these will be relatively minor updates, primarily featuring a faster S12 processor and a few internal upgrades, with no major new health sensors or design changes expected. Read about the Apple Watch Series 12 rumors. 
Apple TV 4K and HomePod Mini
Both the Apple TV 4K and HomePod mini are long overdue for an update and are expected to launch this fall. The delay has reportedly been due to Apple waiting for the new Siri AI architecture to be ready. The new models are expected to feature more powerful chips (like the A17 Pro in the Apple TV) to support the full Siri AI experience, enabling more contextual and conversational interactions. Read about Apple’s HomePod plans.
Software
Apple is also likely to announce the date when it will release the new iOS 27 and watchOS 27 operating systems, most likely a few days after the event. iPadOS 27 and the new macOS Golden Gate may launch alongside iOS 27, but there have been years when these updates were available later. Apple is also likely to reveal when the next updates to tvOS and HomePod software will be available. 
Release dates: New OS download dates
The following launch dates are likely to be announced at the iPhone 17 event:
Monday, September 14: Downloads begin for iOS 26. If you do want to update your iPhone and you are looking for advice on how to install it read: How to update iOS on your iPhone.
Friday, September 11 or Saturday, September 12: iPhone 18 Pro and new Apple Watch preorders begin.
Friday, September 18: iPhone 18 Pro and new Apple Watch models are available for purchase.
Where to watch the iPhone event
Apple will broadcast the event live on its website, the TV app, and on Apple’s YouTube channel. If you want to refresh your memory, the 2025 keynote event is embedded above.
Will the iPhone event be live?
Apple hasn’t held a truly live event since September 2019. Instead, it shows a prerecorded video at the time a live event would be and often holds a small hands-on area to showcase the new products. It is likely that this will once again be the case in 2026, with members of the press gathering at Apple Park to watch the same video Apple will show to the rest of the world.
Interested to find out what won’t launch at the September event? Read: The iPhone event is September 9. The iPhone you want might not be there.

title: The iPhone event is September 9. The iPhone you want might not be there
content:
Macworld





Apple’s fall iPhone event has become one of the easiest product launches to predict. Every year since 2011, we’ve gotten the full lineup of new iPhones, joined in 2014 by the Apple Watch, and occasionally a related launch like AirPods or Apple Pay. 
We now know that the event will be held on Wednesday, September 9. However, according to strong rumors, this year’s keynote will be quite different from previous ones. While it will still be an Phone event, only the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and the long-rumored foldable iPhone Ultra, are expected to be announced, along with the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4.
That means there will be a lot of disappointed Apple fans this year. Here’s what’s not coming—and when to expect it to arrive.
Don’t expect the full iPhone 18 family
For years, Apple has announced every flagship iPhone model at the same event in September. But that seems set to change this year as Apple both expands and shifts its iPhone lineup to welcome new models.
Multiple reports suggest Apple is splitting its iPhone roadmap into two launch windows. Premium models, including the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, and the foldable iPhone Ultra, are expected to debut this September. The standard iPhone 18, however, is rumored to arrive several months later, likely alongside the spot usually reserved for the iPhone 18e.

				
					

				
			
Screenshot

Apple




This would mark a major shift in Apple’s strategy and will make the September keynote much more of a “Pro” event than a simple iPhone event as we know it today.
From Apple’s perspective, the move makes sense. Launching six phones at once inevitably means some products receive far less attention than others. Separating the lineup gives Apple two opportunities each year to dominate the smartphone conversation while also simplifying manufacturing and supply chain logistics.
For buyers, though, it creates a different problem. If you’re interested in Apple’s more affordable phones, the September keynote may not have much to offer. That means you’ll probably have to wait much longer to buy the phone you want.
No iPhone Air 2 just yet
Another notable omission from this year’s September keynote is likely to be the iPhone Air. Apple spent a lot of time talking about its new ultra-thin iPhone last year. This time, however, rumors suggest that we won’t see a new Air alongside the new iPhone 18 Pro and Ultra.
Instead, Apple reportedly plans to keep the current iPhone Air on the market for a few more months before introducing a new iPhone Air in the spring with the 18 and 18e. Since this is the first update, this would put the Air on a slower update cycle, more similar to products like the iPad Pro, rather than the standard iPhone lineup, though it’s unclear whether the 3rd-gen model would arrive next spring or the following fall.
A longer update cadence makes sense if you consider what the Air represents. It’s less about chasing annual performance gains and more about offering a unique design for people who prioritize thinness above everything else. Also, according to multiple sources, Apple is still exploring ways to improve the iPhone Air’s hardware in light of the model’s low sales figures.

				
					

				
			
The Apple Watch SE 3 will likely stick around for another year.

Chris Martin / Foundry




The next Apple Watch SE skips another year
Another Apple product that doesn’t follow a regular update cycle is the Apple Watch SE. Last year, Apple updated its most affordable smartwatch with the latest chip and an always-on display, while keeping the same Series 4-based design introduced with the original Apple Watch SE in 2020.
Those waiting for a new version of the Apple Watch SE will likely have to wait another year, as there are no rumors of a new SE model coming out this fall. That’s not a surprise, as Apple has never updated the Apple Watch SE in back-to-back years.
At $249, the Apple Watch SE is still an easy recommendation for first-time Apple Watch buyers, but it’s becoming increasingly hard to ignore just how outdated it looks compared to the flagship models.
Exciting announcements coming this fall
Although it may seem that this year’s September event might feature fewer products than usual, it’s still shaping up to be the most exciting iPhone event in years.
Apple is reportedly preparing its biggest iPhone shake-up in years with the debut of the foldable iPhone Ultra, while the iPhone 18 Pro models are expected to introduce new camera hardware and other refinements. There are also expected to be a new Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4, as well as new Siri AI features reserved for the new devices.

				
					

				
			
Apple is likely launching is first folding phone in September.

Foundry




There could be some surprises too. A recent leak revealed that Apple is preparing to introduce new AirPods models at the iPhone event, including an entirely new version with built-in cameras to enable AI features. Apple could also use the event to launch its long-rumored smart home push, including the so-called HomePad home hub as well as a new Apple TV 4K and HomePod mini.
Finally, Apple is also working on a new iPad mini with an OLED display and a faster chip, as well as an Apple Intelligence update to the entry-level iPad, either of which could make an appearance at the September event.
But if you’ve been holding out for an iPhone 18, iPhone 18e, iPhone Air 2, or a new Apple Watch SE, you may need to keep waiting just a little longer. That’s becoming the new normal for Apple: Fewer products per keynote, but more launches spread throughout the year.

title: Leaked Images Give First Look at Apple's AI Servers
content:
Images claiming to show the inside of an Apple-made AI server, believed to power Private Cloud Compute, surfaced online this week, offering a first look at how the hardware is laid out.


The images were shared earlier this week by the X user @hsuchingpo, an account with a track record of Apple hardware and prototype leaks. Captioned simply "Apple M5 Server," the leaker said the hardware is "most likely" Apple's Private Cloud Compute (PCC) system. Private Cloud Compute is Apple's system for offloading demanding Apple Intelligence requests from a device to the cloud while keeping user data from being stored or shared.

The images show a rack mountable chassis packed with compute modules. Each one has a separate circuit board mounted on a carrier bar and secured with blue and red ejector latches for quick removal. The boards connect into a backplane through gold edge connectors, with heatsinks running through the center of each column and a service diagram taped inside the lid mapping out numbered board positions and Apple part numbers.


苹果M5服务器#apple pic.twitter.com/BJE4W0qPWF
— 徐静环境 (@hsuchingpo) August 24, 2026
 


Each single chassis holds up to 32 boards. The layout appears to be built around airflow, with heatsinks running down the center and fans at both ends. 

One close-up image shows a board with its thermal paste wiped away, revealing an Apple logo printed directly onto a chip package, appearing to confirm the hardware uses Apple's own silicon. Two NAND flash chips sit nearby.

title: When is Apple’s next event? Dates, rumors, and what to expect
content:
Macworld





Apple has confirmed the date of its next event: this year’s September event will take place on Wednesday, September 9. It may not be Apple’s final event of 2026, however, with another launch potentially following in October.
Apple typically has four main event windows each year: a spring event, WWDC in June, the iPhone event in September, and sometimes a further event in October. The company rarely confirms dates far in advance, and there’s no guarantee it will hold an event in every window. That leaves Apple fans – and anyone considering a new Apple device – wondering when the next event will happen and what might be announced.
Fortunately, Apple’s annual schedule is fairly predictable, while reliable rumours often provide additional clues about what’s coming. That means we can make informed estimates about the timing of future keynotes and the products most likely to appear.
From the iPhone 18 lineup and new Apple Watches to potential Mac and iPad updates, here’s everything we know about Apple’s next event, along with the other events Apple could hold in 2026 and beyond.


When is Apple’s next event?
Wednesday September 9, 2026
Apple announced the date of it’s September event on August 26, two weeks before the event is scheduled to be held on September 9. 
Based on Apple’s typical event schedule, we had already predicted that the annual iPhone launch would take place on this date. September 9 was the most likely date because September 7 is labor day and Apple would not usually hold an event the day after a public holiday. 
Earlier in August the company asked Apple Store staff to apply for an “Event Support Experience Program” to enter a lottery for the opportunity to assist with an Apple event scheduled for the first half of September.
As in previous years, Apple is expected to livestream the event, allowing viewers around the world to watch the company unveil its latest products. One notable change this year is that the keynote is expected to be hosted by John Ternus, who is set to succeed Tim Cook as Apple’s CEO following Cook’s retirement.


						

							




Apple event calendar 2026

March Special Experience2-4 MarchLaunched: iPhone 17e, MacBooks Neo, Pro & Air, iPad Air

October or November[Late fall event]TBCPossible: Macs and iPads

Apple has held two events so far in 2026, although the first was not an event in the traditional sense. On March 4, the company invited select media to hands-on “experiences” in multiple locations. In the run-up to that date, Apple also launched several products via press release, including the iPhone 17e, M4 iPad Air, and MacBook Pro M5 Pro and M5 Max, M5 MacBook Air and the MacBook Neo.
The second event was WWDC, which began with a keynote on June 8. At the WWDC keynote Apple outlined the upcoming changes to its operating systems, including iOS 27 and macOS 27 Golden Gate.
Looking ahead to the fall, Apple is expected to unveil the iPhone 18 Pro, a foldable iPhone Ultra, and more at an Apple event on September 9.
A second, late-fall event in October or November is possible, though less certain and typically focused on Macs or iPads.

				
					

				
			
Here’s when the 2026 Apple events might take place.

Foundry





 FAQ 


1.
What will Apple announce at the next event?
Apple’s September event is the biggest and most watched Apple event of the year. It’s the venue at which Apple unveils the new iPhones and Apple Watches for the next year. 
We expect Apple to launch the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and Apple Watch Series 12 at a September event. Apple may also reveal the new folding iPhone, thought to be called the iPhone Ultra.
Rumors also point to a new and improved HomePod and Apple TV. The iPad and iPad mini are also overdue an update so may arrive at the same event.
We may also see updates to the Mac Studio and Mac mini.





2.
What time does the next Apple event start in U.S., U.K. and other global time zones
Apple keynotes usually start at 10 am PT and this one is no different. That translates to the following times in the countries where most of our readers live:
U.S.: 10 am PDT, 11 am MDT, 12 pm CDT, 1 pm EDT
Canada: as above, plus 2 pm ADT
