title: My daughter brought a Mac to college. This is the tech I wish I’d packed for her
content:
Macworld





Going to college or university is the first long-term stay away from home for most new students. Alongside the really boring stuff—bedding, clothes hangers, notepads, and coffee cups—there’s a lot of new tech to take, and most freshmen miss some of the electronic essentials that they all will need from day one in their college dorm.
You know that you’ll need a computer—most likely a portable laptop, and we recommend the best MacBook for students elsewhere. Many students—particularly those studying science subjects—find a tablet such as an Apple iPad is more convenient, and so you can read our list of the best iPads for students, too. Indeed, with the addition of a supporting keyboard, the iPad can also function as well as laptops for written assessments: see our recommendations for the best iPad keyboards.
We surveyed a bunch of second-year students and their parents to come up with this list of the essential tech and gadgets every student needs in their room and for going about their daily college life.
Charging station
The number-one forgotten electronic item when heading off to college is the humble charging station, power strip, or plug extension cord. Dorm rooms—some designed before smartphones and even laptops existed—have precious few power sockets, and the one you eventually find is sure to be located as far away as possible from where you need it. A power strip will solve nearly all a student’s room’s charging problems. Look for one with a cord of at least six feet since power outlets are always in the wrong spot.
Rather than just plugging in a standard long power strip, choose a power extender with USB ports—select one with more USB-C than older USB-A type ports, plus a handful of AC power outlets just like those on a wall socket. USB-C is the more modern connector and is required for fast charging of your iPhone, iPad and MacBook as well as many other powered items.

				
					

				
			
Baseus




U.S. students/parents should consider the Baseus EnerFill FD11 Power Strip (pictured above) that boasts six AC power outlets for larger items (kettle, printer, lamps and TV), three USB-C ports (for smartphones and tablets) and a legacy USB-A port for your older tech. Each USB-C port can handle 67W of power, which is enough power to keep a MacBook Air or a 14-inch MacBook Pro filled up.

				
					

				
			
Anker




Another option is the Anker Nano Power Strip desk clamp (above) that hosts six AC outlets, two that come up on top of the desk while the others are hidden underneath. There are two USB-C ports and two USB-A ports easily accessible above your desk too. One of the USB-C ports delivers up to 70W, which is enough to fast-charge most laptops, along with iPhones and iPads. The desk needs to be no thinner than 0.6 inches and no thicker than 1.8 inches, which you might not know until you get to your college room. The Baseus Power Strip is maybe less neat but more flexible.

				
					

				
			
Ugreen




U.K. parents/students should consider our previous favorite power strip, the Ugreen 100W USB-C GaN Charging Station (shown above) that is now available only in that region. It features three USB-C ports (2x 100W and 1x 22.5W), one USB-A (22W), and three extra AC plug sockets. That should be enough for most people. If not, buy two. The 100W USB-C ports can charge even a large laptop with ease. Ugreen has a smaller cube-shaped power extender, too: the 65W USB-C GaN Charging Station, with two USB-C (both 65W) and two USB-A (18W) ports, and three AC outlets.

				
					

				
			
Anker




Long cables
All of your Apple devices use USB-C, but you might still have some USB-A and MicroUSB devices around. Also, it’s a common misconception that all USB-C cables are basically the same, but they’re not. Some are for data transfer only. And those that do support charging vary in how fast they can charge. iPhones and tablets require around 30W of power for fast charging, while a MacBook Pro needs 60-100W. The easiest solution is to choose a universal cable that supports up to 100W so you can use it with all your devices.
We recommend the 100W Anker USB-C to USB-C Cable, which is available in black, silver, or red, and in lengths of up to 10 feet. I have a few of these at home, and I bought my daughter two for college. You can buy them singularly for around $10 or in packs of two or three.
That cable will also transfer data, but slowly at 480Mbps. For both speedy data transfers and charging, the most dependable solution is a Thunderbolt or USB4 cable. These look and work just like USB-C but offer superior data speeds for MacBooks and the iPad Pro. The $19/£20 Ugreen USB4 USB-C to USB-C Cable is 3.3-feet long and offers as fast charging support as you can get (240W) and super-speedy data (80Gbps). Longer Thunderbolt cables cost a lot more: the Belkin 6.6ft Thunderbolt 4 Cable costs around $75/£75.
Some older iPhones, AirPods, and iPads use Apple’s Lightning connector, so you need a USB-C to Lightning cable. For a long Lightning cable, try the 10-foot Amazon Basics USB-C to Lightning Cable ($14 / £11) available in either black or white. Anker has a slightly shorter 6-foot Lightning Cable for $25 / £24 that we’d recommend for its better durability and brighter color options (black, silver, red, and gold).

				
					

				
			
Ugreen




WiFi isn’t always great in halls or at the top floor of a shared house, but if the router or network/LAN port is close enough to hand, you can connect your device via Ethernet. Buy for the latest fast networks with a Cat 8 Ethernet cable (you don’t have to know what that is but it’s new and backwards compatible with older networks). Ugreen’s Ethernet Cable comes in a range of lengths, and prices start at just $6.99 / £8.99. If your laptop doesn’t have an Ethernet port Ugreen has a USB-C to Ethernet adapter you can plug it into for around ten bucks or £12.

				
					

				
			
Simon Jary




Extra power adapters
It’s seems obvious, but extra power adapters are the easiest thing to forget—and even if you remember, you’ll want to get the right one. You’ll be looking for chargers with at least one USB-C port—some have two or more to be even more useful. The more ports a charger has, the fewer chargers you’ll need to bring.
The $69 Anker Prime 100W USB-C Wall Charger (or £60 at Amazon UK) has three ports (two USB-C and one USB-A) and is small enough to fit in a pocket if you want to carry it with you. We’ve found an even cheaper (but larger) charger, the $55 Ugreen Nexode 200W USB-C Wall Charger (or £89 at Amazon UK) that has four ports (3x USB-C and 1x USB-A) and can pump out up to 200W at the same time.
Those two wall chargers plug directly into a power socket, whether that be in the wall or on a power strip. You can also buy chargers meant to sit on a desk with one long cord to the wall socket. The $79/£79 Anker Prime Charger (200W, 6 Ports, GaN) (also at Amazon and Amazon U.K.) has six ports—4x USB-C and 2x USB-A—and can handle more power (200W) at one time.
If you really just need one port, then USB-C wall chargers come in very small sizes—small enough to lose in your backpack if taking it to keep your laptop or phone charged in the lecture hall. Take a look at the tiny $29/£24 Anker Nano Charger (at Amazon and Amazon U.K.), which can power a laptop at 65W and measures about 1.6 inches cubed.
How to get a student discount at Apple’s Education Store
Wireless charger

				
					

				
			
Simon Jary




Since every college student reaches for their iPhone as soon as they wake up, a wireless charging stand is another student priority tech essential. All iPhones 12 and newer will be compatible with a magnetic wireless charging stand, which can double as an alarm clock when they’re on a nightstand.
One of the easiest to pack is the Kuxiu Folding 3-in-1 Charging Station, which is small enough to fit in your pocket. The $65 / £79 Qi2 version charges the iPhone at 15W, while the $79 / £79 Qi2.2 version is faster at 25W (only 15W for iPhones 15 or older). Both charge the iPhone, Apple Watch, and AirPods at the same time. If they just need to charge an iPhone, look at the simple Anker MagGo Charging Stand ($39/£39).

				
					

				
			
Twelve South




Laptop stand
MacBooks are great, but they’re not exactly designed for comfort and a healthy posture, especially when at a desk. A simple solution is to place your laptop on a pile of books, but a better option is to invest in a laptop stand, which will also increase airflow for better cooling and performance. We’ve tested the best MacBook stands—they’ll work with any laptop—and we have a few favorites.
The $19 / £25 Twelve South Curve SE (pictured above) is an inexpensive but stylish stand that elevates your screen 6.5 inches to a healthier, more ergonomic height. It’s a lightweight modular design that makes it easy to pack for the journey to and from college. 
A more portable laptop stand is the portable, lightweight, and folding $60/£60 Rain Design Mbar Pro+ that raises your MacBook by 5.5 inches with a tilt that makes viewing and typing a more pleasant and healthy experience. When folded, it measures just 0.5 inches thin and weighs 0.45lbs—perfect for slinging in your backpack and taking to the library or café. It even includes its own svelte carrying sleeve.

				
					

				
			
Twelve South




Extra display
A MacBook’s screen is fine for everyday work, but even the 16-inch MacBook Pro can feel small when working with multiple apps and windows open. Having a second larger monitor will make your screen time much more comfortable, productive, and enjoyable, especially when streaming movies. We’ve tested and reviewed the best portable Mac monitors for you.
The ASUS ZenScreen MB249C portable monitor costs $349 or £299 and gives a lot of screen space at 24 inches, but folds into a flat transportable package. Even smaller at 15.6 inches and cheaper ($239), the espresso Lite 15 is also a great pick if you’re worried about packing light, and comes with a fantastic flexible magnetic stand. Both connect to your laptop via a simple USB-C cable and can be closed and stored away when you don’t need them clogging up your desk. 
A cheaper option is to buy a standard computer monitor. The BenQ GW2491 is a bare-bones 24-inch HD monitor that will get the job done for around $99/£75. For a full range of Mac display choices, check out our best monitors roundup.

				
					

				
			
NexiGo




Projector
Who wants to huddle around a small screen when you can beam the latest Netflix hit show into a dorm room wall? While high-quality projectors can run thousands of dollars, budget projectors can be an affordable option for college. The stylish XGIMI Vibe One ($249 / £219) offers a good picture and is also portable with a 1.2-hour battery life so you can take it from your room to the dorm kitchen or to a friend’s house to enjoy your favorite streamers.
Further up the price scale is the $279 NexiGo PJ40 (Gen 3) (or £329 at Amazon UK) that is still less expensive than most but offers vibrant images in light-controlled environments with built-in 20W speakers. To get the best picture in rooms that you can’t sufficiently darken, you’ll have to spend more than $500 on a quality projector such as the Epson Home Cinema.

				
					

				
			
Logitech




Mouse and keyboard
MacBooks obviously come with their own keyboard and trackpad built in, but who doesn’t prefer a more comfortable setup when they’re up all night writing term papers? We suggest you take a look at our roundup of the best Mac keyboards, but here are a few options to get started.
The slimline but solidly built Logitech MX Keys S For Mac is available in either space gray or pale gray for $129/£109), or there’s a more compact version for $99/£70. It’s cheaper than $100-plus Apple’s Magic Keyboard and also more versatile, as it includes a dedicated set of buttons that allow you to pair it with three separate devices, including another Mac, iPad, or even a Windows PC if you really must.
If you want to add a touch of color to your student dorm, consider the Pop Icon series also from Logitech (pictured above), which comes in graphite/green, graphite/white, lilac/off-white, off-white/orange, and rose/off-white. According to the manufacturer, the keyboard has a battery life of up to 36 months, which is most of their college career. You can pick up the mouse and keyboard combo for $66/£69.
For mouse options, check out our recommendations for the best Mac mouse. We recommend the $30/£30 Satechi USB-C Aluminum M1 Bluetooth Wireless Mouse, which comes with a handy scroll wheel for faster, more accurate scrolling and tracking. It has a pleasingly curved ergonomic design made for both left- and right-handed users, and is available in five colors.

				
					

				
			
Logitech




If you decide to go with an iPad instead of a laptop for its note-taking fortitude, you can pick up a keyboard and trackpad for it to make it behave like a laptop when you need to write longer assessments.
Apple’s Magic Keyboard is great, but very expensive. One affordable option is the Zagg Pro Keys that offers a combination of a robust protective case and a removable keyboard at $100/£89 that turns an iPad into a laptop setup and is also effective at protecting it from knocks and drops. A more flexible but still protective solution would be the excellent Logitech Flip Folio Keyboard Case (pictured above) that costs $160/£159 and can be removed simply and quickly.
As with any iPad accessory, make sure you are buying for the model that you own! Apple’s iPad naming convention can make this quite tricky!

				
					

				
			
Plugable




Dock or USB-C hub
Laptops are made much more adaptable by connecting them to a docking station that offers more USB ports, HDMI, card readers and Ethernet for more stable network performance (if the student room includes an Ethernet connection, of course). The $49 Plugable 9-in-1 USB-C Hub Multiport Adapter includes two USB-C ports, three USB-A, HDMI, Gigabit Ethernet, SD, and MicroSD card readers, with 125W laptop charging.
Otherwise, picking one depends on the needs of your student, and there are more Mac USB-C hubs and USB-C and Thunderbolt dock options to choose from.
iPad stylus
Using a stylus makes iPad use even more intuitive than a laptop. The Apple Pencil USB-C is a great option for under $100, but if you’re under a strict budget, the Zagg Pro Stylus 2 ($54/£53) is a more affordable alternative to the Apple Pencil with many of the same features, including wireless charging, a replaceable tip, and attaching magnetically to the iPad Air and iPad Pro.

				
					

				
			
Dominik Tomaszewski / Foundry




Power bank
When out and about, a portable power bank is indispensable for keeping your devices charged when your kid isn’t in their room. For iPhones, we suggest a magnetic power bank that can wirelessly charge your iPhone without a cable. From our long list of the best magnetic power banks, we recommend the EcoFlow RAPID Magnetic Power Bank in either its higher-capacity 10K model ($90) or smaller, lighter 5K version ($40). A cheaper option is the magnetic Baseus PicoGo Power Bank, available in a range of colors for $30/£29.
If you frequently forget to charge your laptop and don’t have a readily available power socket or charger where you go to study, consider a battery pack for your laptop; read about the best power banks for MacBook. A great value 20K laptop power bank is the $30/£27 Cuktech 20K that might be a little slow at 45W, but should get your kid out of a crisis. Or try the faster (67W) Baseus EnerCore CR11 at around $40.

				
					

				
			
Freepik




Laptop bag
Your student will definitely need a decent bag to carry their laptop back and forth from lectures or the library. I say this even though my daughter insisted on carrying her 15-inch MacBook Air around in her completely unsuitable, oversized handbag. The 30-liter Stubble & Co Roll Top I bought her, despite its excellent laptop compartment and good looks, was instead used to drag her shopping back to the residence halls. If they’re like my daughter and don’t want a laptop backpack, then at least consider a laptop sleeve to protect it on its travels.
If you are shopping at Apple there’s a summer-long Back to school deal where you can get a gift card worth up to $150 with your purchase of a Mac or iPad. For advice about how to shop at Apple’s Education store read: How to get an Apple student discount at Apple’s Education Store.

				
					

				
			
Sihoo




Office chair
Last but definitely not least, investing in a decent ergonomic chair is a wise decision for parents but we suspect it will be mostly used by students as an open wardrobe to throw clothes over.
Sihoo is running back-to-school deals on its Sihoo Doro C300 office chair that will give proper support when the student is sat doing some college work.

title: Every Surge Has Character: This collaboration between UNIQ and PANTONE® explores how one color can express different sides of who we are
content:
Macworld





		
Switch up your look for different outfits and occasions
Express different sides of who you are
View Now
Color has never been a fixed thing. It shifts with light, with mood, with the hour of the day and the version of ourselves we bring to it. A single shade of blue can read as calm at breakfast and bold by nightfall. It’s this idea that identity is never singular—that sits at the heart of UNIQ’s new collaboration with PANTONE®: the Revix IV PANTONE® Edition Reversible Apple Watch Band.
On the surface, it’s a watch strap. Look closer, and it’s an argument about how we dress to reflect our different moods, perspectives, and sides of who we are.

				
					

				
			
UNIQ




The problem with one-sided design
Most accessories ask you to commit. One color, one texture, one mood, worn on repeat until it either becomes a signature or starts to feel stale. For a generation that moves fluidly between a client meeting, a gallery opening, and a Sunday run, that kind of rigidity feels increasingly out of step. The Revix IV starts from a different premise: that an everyday essential should flex the way a day actually does.
Its dual-color construction, finished with subtle PANTONE®-informed patterning, gives wearers up to eight distinct ways to style the band, yet in a minimalistic manner. A flip changes the entire register of the piece—from quiet and considered to unexpectedly playful—without changing the object itself. It’s the same idea PANTONE® has spent decades championing: that color is never neutral, it’s a language, and fluency in it means knowing when to switch tone.

				
					

				
			
UNIQ




Function first, always
None of this would matter if the mechanics didn’t hold up, and this is where UNIQ’s engineering does the quiet work behind the design story. A patented connector system makes the transformation between styles genuinely seamless—no tools, no fuss, just a twist and a new look. For those who want an added layer of confidence, optional matching loops reinforce the fit while doubling down on the strap’s dual-colour personality rather than hiding it.
Security, too, has been treated as non-negotiable. The upgraded magnetic attachment has been tested to withstand up to 1.3kg of pull—a reassurance for anyone who has ever felt an Apple Watch strap loosen mid-commute and wondered if their watch would survive the day. Length adjustment stays effortless, so the fit is exact rather than approximate.
Then there’s the part you feel before you see: a soft, leather-like exterior paired with a smooth, finely textured interior. It’s a small detail, but it’s the kind that separates an accessory worn out of habit from one worn with intention—comfortable enough for a twelve-hour day, refined enough not to announce itself.

				
					

				
			
UNIQ




More than a color
What makes this collaboration worth paying attention to isn’t the novelty of a reversible watch strap—plenty of brands have tried variations on that idea. It’s the thinking underneath it. UNIQ × PANTONE® isn’t simply pairing a product with a trusted color authority for credibility’s sake. It’s using color as a genuine design language, one that acknowledges that the people wearing it are not one thing, all the time.

				
					

				
			
UNIQ




UNIQ Blue Surge (above) is the key PANTONE® color representing the UNIQ × PANTONE® collaboration. 
For design-aware professionals building a wardrobe of considered essentials, for students and young creatives testing out identity through what they wear, for anyone who simply wants an Apple Watch strap that won’t quit on them halfway through the day—the Revix IV offers something rare: an object built for change, without ever compromising on reliability, and offering affordability at just $39.90.
Flip it. Match it. Wear it. Every surge, after all, has character—the question is simply which side of yours shows up today.

title: Best MacBook for students: Which Mac should you buy for school or university?

Thinking of buying a Mac or MacBook for school, college or university? Choosing the right one in 2026 isn’t as simple as picking the cheapest model. Apple’s lineup now includes everything from the low-cost MacBook Neo to lightweight MacBooks, powerful Pro machines, and even desktop Macs – all with different strengths depending on your course, workload, and budget.
Whether you’re writing essays, coding, editing video, or just need a reliable laptop for lectures, the best choice depends on how you plan to use it. In this guide, we break down the best Mac for every type of student – from budget buyers to creative pros – compare the MacBook Air and MacBook Pro, and explore whether a desktop Mac might actually be a smarter option for some.
We’ll also help you choose based on your subject and budget, and show you how to save money. Students can take advantage of Apple’s Education Store discounts, and until August 27 (in the U.S.) there are additional savings thanks to Apple’s Back to School offer, where qualifying products come with a gift card for up to $150/£120. It’s worth checking resellers too, where you may find even better deals.
Note that on June 26, 2026 Apple increased Mac prices both for general consumers and for students. You can find the new prices and the savings in the students savings section. 
What is the best Mac for students? 
We’ve picked out the best Macs for students right now, including the MacBook Neo, the latest MacBook Air and Pro models, and even desktop alternatives like the Mac mini. Here are our top recommendations based on price, performance and what most students actually need.

The MacBook Air is the ideal laptop for most students, offering an excellent balance of portability, battery life, and performance. With the introduction of the M5 chip in early 2026, it further strengthens its position as a dependable everyday “workhorse” for academic and light creative use.
You might assume the MacBook Air is significantly less powerful than the MacBook Pro, but that’s not entirely the case. The entry-level MacBook Pro uses the same M5 chip, meaning day-to-day performance is very similar. The Pro does offer additional advantages, such as improved cooling, more ports and a higher-end display, which we’ll explore in more detail below.
Why the MacBook Air is a good choice for students
The MacBook Air’s biggest advantage is its lightweight, fanless design. It’s easy to carry between classes and operates completely silently – ideal for lectures, libraries, and study spaces. Combined with all-day battery life, it’s well-suited to students who spend long hours away from power outlets. 
MacBook Air offers the following benefits: 
Portability: The 13-inch model weighs under 3 pounds (1.24 kg), making it easy to carry all day.
Silent operation: The fanless design means no noise, even under moderate workloads.
Battery life: Up to 18 hours battery life means students can often leave the charger at home and the MacBook Air can last for the while working day.
Which students is the MacBook Air best for?
The MacBook Air is the mainstream choice for students who want a reliable, versatile laptop without the cost or weight of a Pro model. It’s ideal for:
General students: Writing, research, lectures, and productivity apps (Office, Google Workspace).
Mobile users: Those constantly moving between classes, libraries, and cafés.
Creative students: The 15-inch model is a good fit for light design, editing, or multitasking where Pro-level power isn’t required.
Budget-conscious buyers: M5 starts at $1,299 ($1,199 education), while older models (M4) often offer excellent value on sale.
MacBook Air performance for student workloads
While the MacBook Pro is designed for sustained, high-end professional workloads, the MacBook Air delivers more than enough performance for the majority of students, including:
Everyday tasks: Smooth handling of web browsing (even with many tabs), document work, and streaming.
Creative work: The M5 chip adds improved graphics performance, including enhanced shader cores and ray tracing, making it capable of light video editing and 3D work.
MacBook Air specs
Processor (CPU/GPU): The M5 chip features a 10-core CPU and up to a 10-core GPU.
Memory (RAM): As of late 2024, Apple began shipping all models with a minimum of 16GB of RAM. For students looking at older or refurbished models, experts recommend a minimum of 16GB to ensure longevity and smooth multitasking.
13-inch or 15-inch Display: Liquid Retina display with 500 nits brightness and strong color accuracy – great for both study and creative use.
Storage (SSD): The base storage for the M5 model has doubled to 512GB. This is particularly beneficial for students who need to store large project files, though those on a budget can still find older 256GB models sufficient if paired with cloud storage.
MacBook Air tradeoffs 
Choosing the Air over the MacBook Pro or the budget-friendly MacBook Neo involves several specific tradeoffs regarding sustained power, display technology, and port selection.
Performance and Thermal Management: The most significant technical tradeoff is the Air’s fanless design. While this makes the laptop completely silent, it limits performance during long, intensive tasks.
Refresh Rate: The Air is limited to a 60Hz refresh rate, missing the 120Hz ProMotion technology found on the Pro.
Brightness and HDR: It lacks the HDR capabilities and extreme brightness levels of the Liquid Retina XDR displays.
Audio: The 13-inch Air uses a four-speaker system, whereas the 15-inch Air and MacBook Pro models offer superior six-speaker systems with force-canceling woofers.
Connectivity and Ports: MacBook Air is designed for portability, which results in a more limited selection of physical ports compared to the Pro.

Why the MacBook Neo is a good choice for students
The MacBook Neo’s biggest advantage is value. It delivers a premium-feeling Mac experience at a significantly lower cost, making it especially appealing to students on a tight budget.
MacBook Neo offers the following benefits:
Affordability: Starts at $699 ($599 education), making it the cheapest Mac you can buy right now (although it previously cost $100 less).
Performance: Powered by the A18 Pro chip, offering fast single-core performance for everyday tasks.
Build quality: All-aluminum design that feels closer to a MacBook Air than typical budget laptops.
Battery life: Up to 16 hours – enough for a full school day.

Apple ecosystem: Seamless integration with iPhone features like iPhone Mirroring, Universal Clipboard, and iCloud.
Design: Available in multiple colors, including silver, indigo, blush, and citrus.
Which students is the MacBook Neo best for?
The MacBook Neo is ideal for students who want a reliable, well-built laptop for everyday use without paying for higher-end performance. It’s ideal for:
K–12 and first-time users: A great entry-level device for schoolwork and general productivity.
Budget-conscious college students: A strong option for those who want macOS at a lower price.
Casual creative learners: Suitable for beginners exploring tools like Adobe apps without heavy workloads.
Apple ecosystem users: Best for students who already use an iPhone or other Apple devices.
The MacBook Neo is best suited for students with simple, everyday computing needs. For more demanding workflows – such as advanced video editing, 3D work, or software development – the MacBook Air (M5) or MacBook Pro models remain better choices.
MacBook Neo performance for student workloads
The MacBook Neo is optimized for typical student use and handles everyday tasks with ease, including:
Everyday tasks: Smooth performance for web browsing, email, documents, and streaming.
Light creative work: Capable of basic photo and video editing (including 1080p and light 4K), though not designed for sustained professional workloads.
MacBook Neo specs 
As a low-priced device so the specs are basic, but should be enough to handle the “day-to-day stuff” essential for schoolwork, such as writing papers, browsing, and streaming. 
Processor: An A18 Pro or A19 Pro chip (depending on the specific model year), which provides excellent single-core performance for a smooth operating system feel.
Memory: 8GB of unified memory, which is the maximum available for this model.
Storage: Options for a 256GB or 512GB SSD.
Battery Life: Up to 16 hours of video playback, which comfortably covers a full school day.
MacBook Neo tradeoffs
To reach its lower price, the MacBook Neo makes several compromises compared to the Air and Pro models, so there are some trade-offs to consider:
Memory: 8GB RAM only, with no upgrade option.
Ports: Two USB-C ports, no Thunderbolt; one limited to USB 2.0 speeds.
Display limitations: Lacks P3 wide color and True Tone, making it less ideal for color-critical work.
Features: No MagSafe, no keyboard backlight, and no Touch ID on the base model.
External display support: Limited to a single external monitor.

Getting a student discount from Apple’s Education Store isn’t the only way to save money when buying a Mac. Here are some other ways to find a good deal:
Look out for reseller discounts

Buy a refurbished Mac
Apple’s Refurbished Store offers ex-display, returned, and previous-generation Macs at reduced prices. These devices are fully tested and come with a one-year warranty, making them a reliable option.
You can also buy refurbished Macs from third-party resellers, though quality can vary – so always check what “refurbished” includes before buying. Read our advice about buying a refurbished Mac, including Pros, cons, savings, and what to avoid.
What to avoid 
Avoid Intel-based Macs: Macs used to use Intel Processors but over the past few years Apple has transitioning to its own silicon (M1, M2, M3, etc.). Only a small number of Intel Macs receive security updates, and that will not continue for long. This could mean needing to upgrade sooner than expected. 
Don’t buy second-hand or used: While used Macs can be cheaper, they come with more risk. Unlike refurbished models, they may not be tested or come with a warranty. If you do consider buying second-hand, proceed with caution and buy from a trusted source.
Consider older models carefully: The biggest discounts are often on older Macs. While these can be good value, make sure you understand how they compare to newer models. Older devices may lack performance improvements, battery efficiency, and long-term software support. See: How long does Apple support Macs for.


						

							





 FAQ 


1.
Is a MacBook Neo good enough for students?
Yes. The MacBook Neo is considered an excellent choice for students with more than enough power for the average student. However, students in specialized fields like engineering, 4K video editing, or heavy software development may find the device limiting. 





2.
Is a MacBook Air good enough for students?
The MacBook Air is the best laptop for most students due to its balance of portability, battery life, and performance. While the Air is “good enough” for the vast majority, a MacBook Pro is better for heavy workloads, connectivity and display tech. 





3.
How much RAM do students need?
8GB should be sufficient for the MacBook Neo, but we recommend 16GB or more for other Macs.





4.
Is 256GB enough storage? 
For most students, 256GB of storage is a functional minimum rather than an ideal long-term solution. It can work if you rely heavily on cloud storage, but many students will find it fills up quickly over time.
256GB is usually enough for basic academic tasks such as writing essays, web browsing, streaming, and light media use. However, modern operating systems and apps take up more space than ever, and storage can fill up faster than expected. Performance can also suffer as a drive nears capacity. A common rule of thumb is to buy at least twice the storage you think you’ll need to allow for growth and maintain performance.
For most students, 512GB is now the practical minimum if your budget allows. It provides more flexibility and longevity, especially as course materials and apps grow in size.





5.
What Apple Intelligence/AI features do Macs have for students?
Apple Intelligence brings a range of AI-powered tools to Macs designed to support academic work – from smarter note-taking to writing assistance and automation. These features are increasingly integrated into everyday apps like Notes, Messages, and Shortcuts. 
Useful features include:
Smart transcription and scanning: Turn lectures and printed text into searchable notes.
In-line maths and handwriting refinement: Solve equations and improve handwritten notes.
Editing and summarisation: Refine essays and condense key information.
Live translation: Translate messages and add captions in calls.
Automation: Use Shortcuts to generate text or images automatically.
While these features can boost productivity, it is important to note that over-reliance on AI for writing could raise plagiarism or originality concerns if not used carefully. 
Not all Apple devices support Apple Intelligence and some features are still less advanced than competing AI platforms. 





How to choose the best MacBook for students 
There is no “best MacBook for students” because everyone has different needs and choosing the best MacBook for a student depends on balancing academic requirements, portability, and budget. With the introduction of the MacBook Neo, Apple has significantly expanded its entry-level options, making the decision more complex than simply picking the most popular model. 
When evaluating which model fits your needs, consider these primary components:
Portability vs. Screen Real Estate: The 13-inch models (Neo, Air, and Pro) weigh under 3 pounds, making them ideal for carrying between lectures. However, creative majors often benefit from the 15-inch Air or 16-inch Pro for more workspace.
Performance Needs: For general coursework (writing papers, browsing, streaming), the A18 Pro or M5 chips are more than sufficient. Students in engineering, data science, or high-end video editing should prioritize the MacBook Pro with M5 Pro or Max chips for sustained performance and better cooling.
Battery Life: This is critical for long days on campus. While the Neo offers up to 16 hours of video streaming, the M5 MacBook Air provides 18 hours, and the 14-inch MacBook Pro leads with up to 24 hours.
Connectivity: The MacBook Neo and Air feature silent, fanless designs but limited ports . The MacBook Pro includes HDMI and SDXC slots, which are useful for presentations and transferring media.
In conclusion, we recommend the following Macs depending on your use case:

Creative & STEM MajorsMacBook Pro (M5/Pro)High-end displays (ProMotion) and power for heavy workloads.
Budget Desktop SetupMac mini (M6)Best value if portability isn’t required; $799 with education discount.

title: Apple Back to School Deal 2026: Students can get up to $150 gift card with purchases
content:
Macworld





Apple runs a higher education promotion every year that has traditionally been known as its “Back to School” sale. The company now refers to it as the “College Student Offer” or “Higher Education Offer” because it is only available to students in higher education and eligible education staff – not school-age children.
The promotion gives eligible customers an extra incentive when purchasing qualifying products through Apple’s Education Store, where Macs and iPads are already sold at discounted prices. In recent years, those incentives have included free AirPods, a free Apple Pencil, and other accessories. This year Apple has returned to the tradition of offering gift cards with purchases – worth up to $150 in 2026. Apple launches the offer at different times around the world to coincide with the university summer break in each region. It typically begins before the new academic year and runs until several weeks after the first term starts.
In 2025, the U.S. promotion began on June 17 and ran until September 30, so a similar launch date had been expected in 2026. Instead, Apple started the promotion on Thursday, July 16, a month later than expected, and originally announced it would end on August 27, a month earlier than in 2025. However, in early August, Apple extended it until September 24. The U.K. promotion started on August 13 and will run until October 22, 2026. 
There had been some speculation that the offer might not return this year – particularly after the company increased Mac and iPad price, citing rising component costs and memory shortages, but Apple is going ahead with the deal. The same promotion is likely to start in the U.K. and Europe before the end of July.


Region2026 Start date2026 End Date2026 Deal

U.K. & Europe August 13, 2026October 22, 2026Confirmed: Gift Cards worth up to £120.
Australia January 7, 2026March 11, 2026Ended: Free/discounted AirPods, Apple Pencil, Keyboards and Mice

 



Read on to find out everything you need to know about Apple’s Higher Education promotion this year, including when it is expected to begin in your region, what products and incentives may be included, who qualifies, and how to take advantage of the offer.
Apple’s “Back to school” deal: At a glance
What is Apple’s “Back to School” deal? The 2026 deal is gift cards worth up to $150/£120 with purchases of qualifying Macs and iPads.
When is Apples “Back to School” deal? It is running from July 16 to September 24, 2026 in North America. In the U.K. and Europe it is running from August 13 to October 22.
Is this the only student saving from Apple? No, Apple offers a discount on Macs and iPads all year round to qualifying students. Read: How to get an Apple student discount at Apple’s Education Store.
Who qualifies? Verified students in higher education institutions – and their parents. 


When does Apple’s “Back to School” deal start?

				
					

				
			
The 2026 promotion

Apple





U.S. & Canada: From July 16 – September 24, 2026. (Gift cards)
U.K. & Europe: August 13 to October 22, 2026. (Gift cards)
India: From July 16 – September 24, 2026. (Apple is giving away AirPods and Apple Pencil in India)
Australia, New Zealand, Brazil and South Korea: January 7 to – early March 11 2026.
In North America, Apple’s annual “College Student Offer” promotion is live now. It started on Thursday, July 16, and finishes on September 24, 2026.
Because the academic summer break begins and ends later in Europe, the promotion launched slightly later in the U.K. and across Europe. There is began on August 13 and will run until October 22. 
The deal ran from January 7 to early March 11 this year in the Southern Hemisphere. 
Similar timings are expected in 2027.


						

							


Who can get Apple’s “Back to School” give-away? 
Current and newly accepted higher education students – and their parents

				
					

				
			
Apple




If you are enrolled at a higher education institution (post-K12 education, such as a university or college), or are the parent of a student who is enrolled, you qualify for Apple’s year-round education pricing as well as the “Back to School” promotion while it is running.
You will need to verify your eligibility before you can access the offer. Prior to May 2026, verifying student status in some countries – including the U.S. – only required an .edu email address and the name of a higher education institution. Apple has since tightened its verification requirements.
As a result, shoppers now need to verify their student status through UNiDAYS (as was already the case in the U.K.). Students are typically required to provide their name, date of birth, and school email address, then search for their institution and wait for their student status to be confirmed.
Apple’s education pricing is not available to parents buying for school-age children, but it is available to parents who are homeschooling their children.


						

							


What is Apple’s “Back to School” deal this year?

				
					

				
			
Get free money with your purchase. 

Foundry





Gift cards worth up to $150/£120 with MacBook Pro, $100/£80 with MacBook Air, iPad Air and iPad Pro.
In India, Apple is giving away AirPods/Apple Pencil/keyboard/mouse were offered with qualifying purchases, as it did for the Australian promotion earlier in 2026.
The free AirPods usually given away with this offer have a value of $129, so the $150 or $100 voucher has an almost equivalent value to that. The gift card does at least give students the freedom to decide how they would like to spend the money.
Typical savings in the education store already include:
$200/£200 off an MacBook Pro
$100/£100 off an MacBook Air
$100/£100 off an iPad Pro
$50/£50 off an iPad Air
$80/£80 off an Apple Watch Ultra 3
$40/£40 off an Apple Watch Series 11
£10/$10 off the Apple Pencil Pro
£10/$10 off the standard Apple Pencil
So the gift card represents a total saving of $350 for the MacBook Pro, $200 off the price of a MacBook Air, and $200 off an iPad Pro, and $150 off an iPad Air. 
This isn’t the first time Apple has offered gift cards. From 2022 to 2024 in the U.S., U.K., and some other regions, Apple instead offered gift cards worth up to $150/£130, depending on the products purchased during the promotional period. 
During the Australian promotion, that ran from January 7 to March 11, 2026, Apple offered free or discounted accessories – including AirPods, AirPods Pro, Apple Pencil models, and Apple Keyboard, Mouse, or Trackpad products – with the purchase of qualifying Macs and iPads. Apple is offering that promotion in India. Some European countries may still get AirPods.
The following products were offered for free or discounted, earlier in 2026:
AirPods 4

Magic Mouse
Magic Trackpad

Apple also offered AirPods giveaways during its 2025 promotion, and, previously, Apple also included a discount for the AirPods Max.
Can students qualify for other savings at Apple?
Yes. Apple’s “Back to School” promotion is not the only education-related discount the company offers. Macs and iPads sold through Apple’s Education Store are discounted year-round, so qualifying students and educational institutions can save on the price of a Mac or iPad at any time of the year.
The summertime Back to School promotion is offered in addition to these ongoing education discounts. We explain everything you need to know about qualifying for Apple’s education pricing – including how much you can save and how to shop through the Apple Education Store – in our Guide to shopping in the Apple Education Store.
If you are unsure which device to buy, we also have guides to the Best Mac for Students and the Best iPad for Students.
Students can also take advantage of the discounted Apple Music Student Plan, which includes access to Apple TV+ at no extra cost. Read: How to get the student deal for Apple Music and free Apple TV+.


						

							


How to get Apple’s “Back to School” deal
In order to get Apple’s “Back to School” Deal you need to purchase a qualifying Mac or iPad from your local Apple Education Store during the promotional period. 
You will need to verify your student status via UNiDAYS, as explained above. 
Visit the Apple Education Store for your region using the links below:

When you purchase a qualifying Mac or iPad, you will then be able to claim the promotional freebie or discounted accessory. 
You can choose which of the giveaway product you want to receive when you make your order. In some cases the freebee comes with an additional cost, we include details of how much more you may need to pay in the tables below.


						

							


Which products qualify for Apple’s “Back to School” deal this year? 

				
					

				
			
Apple’s Back To School deal in 2025.

Apple

Did Apple include the MacBook Neo in the 2026 “Back to School” promotion?
Since the Australian promotion ended, Apple has launched the MacBook Neo, a new laptop aimed specifically at students.
Apple has not included the MacBook Neo in the deal for the U.S., U.K. or anywhere else.
This is no surprise. While the new MacBook is clearly targeted at students, we did not expect Apple to include it in the promotion because of its already relatively low starting price.
Did Apple include the Mac mini in the 2026 “Back to School” promotion?
Apple has previously allowed the purchase of a Mac mini to qualify for the promotion, but not in 2025 or in 2026.
With the launch of a new Mac mini in August 2026, which won’t ship until late September, it’s absence from the promotion is no surprise.
In recent times, the Mac mini has surged in popularity, especially among AI developers looking for a relatively inexpensive Apple Silicon machine capable of handling local AI workloads. This popularity, combined with ongoing global component shortages, has left Mac mini supply severely constrained throughout much of 2026.
Did Apple include the iPad A16 in the 2026 “Back to School” promotion?
Apple has previously allowed entry-level iPads to qualify for its Back to School promotion, but that was not the case in 2025 and it is not the case in 2026.
With a new entry-level iPad expected later in 2026 – and the current iPad A16 lacking support for Apple Intelligence — so our recommendation would be to choose an iPad Air instead.
Did Apple include the iPad mini in the 2026 “Back to School” promotion?
Apple has included the iPad mini in some Back to School promotions in the past. This year it is not included. A new iPad mini is expected to launch in 2026, so we would recommend waiting for that. 
Did Apple include the iPhone in the 2026 “Back to School” promotion?
Apple has never included the iPhone, Apple Watch, or any products other than selected Macs and iPads as qualifying purchases for its “Back to School” promotion.


						

							


How much can you save in Apple’s student deal? 

				
					

				
			
Apple




Students can already save up to $200/£220 on Macs and up to $100/£100 on iPads year-round through Apple’s Education Store. Read more here: How to get an Apple student discount at Apple’s Education Store.
The additional savings available through Apple’s “Back to School” promotion depend on both the product purchased and the promotional accessory being offered.
In previous promotions, students could save up to $199 by choosing a free Magic Keyboard, up to 179 with the AirPods Pro 4 ANC (with the MacBook Pro), up to $129 by selecting AirPods 4, or up to $129 by choosing an Apple Pencil Pro. title: BenQ's New iScreenBar is a Monitor Light Bar Made for the iMac
content:
BenQ today announced the launch of the iScreenBar, which it says is the first monitor light bar built for the iMac.


The iScreenBar is meant to look like an extension of the ‌iMac‌, offering desk lighting that does not clash with the ‌iMac‌'s design or block the camera or microphone. It's made from aluminum and lights an area of 33.5 by 19.7 inches at 500 lux. A glass touch panel is available for adjustments, and there's also a macOS app for tweaking brightness, color temperature, and light mode.

It turns on and off using presence detection and can also activate when the ‌iMac‌ wakes, plus it dims or brightens as the lighting in the room changes. In video call mode, evens lighting and reduces glare on the face for a better image when the camera is in use.


The light bar mounts to the back of the ‌iMac‌ using a magnetic clamp, and it comes with a magnetic cable clip to hide cords. BenQ says asymmetric optics light the user's desk without shining on the screen or in the eyes to reduce glare and preserve color accuracy. It is powered by the ‌iMac‌'s USB-C port, which also allows for automatic camera mode activation.

purchased from BenQ or from Amazon for $189. It is compatible with the 24-inch ‌iMac‌ (2021 and later).

title: Apple Maps Ads Are Here, and There's No Way to Turn Them Off
content:
Ads in Apple Maps are live in the United States and Canada, which means iPhone and iPad users will see them when searching for locations and when viewing Suggested Places.


Apple announced plans to bring ads to the Maps app in March, and said the feature would roll out starting in late summer. Apple confirmed to 9to5Mac that ads began showing up for users over the last few days, with ad placement to ramp up in the coming weeks.

Ads are shown in Suggested Places when initiating a search and after searching if a company has bought an ad for a keyword you're looking for. Ads are shown at the top of search results, with one ad per set of search results.

There is no option to turn off ads in the Maps app, but ads are clearly labeled with a blue "Ad" tag. Apple says ads you interact with in the Maps app are not associated with your Apple Account, and data is not shared with third parties.

content:

Price Increases - The Mac mini now starts at $899, $300 over the original starting price of the M4 Mac mini when it launched in October 2024. Mac Studio pricing starts at $2,499, $500 more than the original price of the M4 Max model when it came out in March 2025.

 	
Connectivity - Apple upgraded the new Macs with Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, so they are on par with the connectivity standards in the latest iPhone models. Wi-Fi 7 offers faster data speeds in the 6GHz band, lower latency, and an option to connect across 2.4GHz, 5GHz, and 6GHz networks at once for reliability improvements.

 	
Genlock - The ‌Mac mini‌ and ‌Mac Studio‌ support genlock over USB-C, so there's no need for a separate sync box. Genlock is used in multi-camera shoots and virtual production to lock timing to a shared reference signal. The Mac's display and the camera filming it are synchronized, preventing flickering and tearing from a mismatch between the display refresh rate and camera shutter. Apple previously added genlock support to the iPhone 17 Pro models, so now an ‌iPhone 17 Pro‌ and one of the new Macs can work in tandem for pros who need the feature.

 	
Ethernet - The ‌Mac mini‌ now starts with 2.5Gb Ethernet instead of 1Gb. There's an option to upgrade to 10Gb, which is what the ‌Mac Studio‌ starts with (same as the prior-generation model).

 	
Neural Engine - The M6 chip has an upgraded Neural Engine with two 16-core engines instead of just one. Apple says the new Neural Engine offers 2x more peak compute so AI workflows run faster.

 	
GPU - The M6 ‌Mac mini‌'s 12-core GPU has Neural Accelerators in each core, offering up to 4x faster AI performance and 2x faster graphics than the ‌M4 Mac mini‌. The ‌Mac Studio‌'s M5 Ultra is also the first Ultra chip with Neural Accelerators. Peak AI compute performance is 4.3x the M3 Ultra's performance.

 	
SSD - ‌Mac Studio‌ storage is twice as fast with new SSD architecture built on PCIe Gen 6.

 	
SSD Pricing - As Daring Fireball points out, upgrading a ‌Mac mini‌ with a 2TB SSD costs $1,000, which is more than the $899 base price of the machine. Upgrading to the 4TB SSD for the M5 Pro costs $1,800, which is $100 over the price of the base machine.

 	
Thunderbolt - The M6 ‌Mac mini‌ continues to have Thunderbolt 4, not Thunderbolt 5. The M5 Pro model does have Thunderbolt 5.

 	
Current Max Pricing - An M5 Pro ‌Mac mini‌ with 18-core CPU, 64GB RAM, an 8TB SSD, and 10GbE is $6,799. The M5 Ultra ‌Mac Studio‌ with 36-core CPU, 256GB RAM, and 16TB SSD is $18,299.

 	
512GB RAM - You can only buy the M5 Ultra with 96GB or 256GB of RAM right now, but a 512GB option is coming in late October. Since upgrading from 96GB RAM to 256GB RAM costs $4,000, the 512GB option will likely cost at least $6,000. 

 	
Announcement Timing - This is the first time Apple has announced new Macs in August since the 27-inch iMac debuted in August 2020.

 	
macOS Golden Gate - When the new machines launch on September 22, they will likely have macOS Golden Gate installed. The software update is probably going to come out the week of September 14.

title: Apple to Release 13 More New Products Later This Year
content:

It is nearly September, and that means the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and the first-ever foldable iPhone are just around the corner. Other products expected later this year include the Apple Watch Series 12 with a ceramic case option, AirPods 5, an all-new Apple home hub, new Apple TV and HomePod mini models, and more.

Apple is expected to release at least 13 more products by the end of 2026, according to rumors. We have provided a summary below.

iPhones


iPhone 18 Pro: A20 Pro chip, a smaller Dynamic Island, a simplified Camera Control button, a Dark Cherry color option, and more.

iPhone 18 Pro Max: The same features rumored for the iPhone 18 Pro, but the Pro Max model may be slightly thicker due to a larger battery and a variable aperture camera, which might be exclusive to the Pro Max model this year.

iPhone Ultra: A foldable iPhone Ultra with a 7.7-inch inner display and 5.3-inch outer display, two rear cameras, one front camera, a Touch ID power button instead of Face ID, and more. iOS 27 is expected to be tailored for the foldable iPhone, allowing for side-by-side apps and other iPad-like multitasking functionality.

Apple Watch Ultra 4: A faster S11 chip or newer, fitness tracking improvements, and additional satellite features for the Apple Watch Ultra 3 and newer, such as Apple Maps via satellite and the ability to send and receive photos with Messages via satellite. iPads

Macs


iMac: M6 chip and new color options.

Home


Apple TV: At least five new features, including an A17 Pro chip or newer, an increased 8GB of RAM for Apple Intelligence, Siri AI support, an Apple-designed N1 chip with Wi-Fi 7 support, and an updated Siri Remote.

HomePod mini: Newer chip with Siri AI support, improved sound quality, Apple's N1 chip with Wi-Fi 7 support, a second-generation Ultra Wideband chip, and potentially new color options like red.

Wild Card

title: New Mac Studio M5 Max and M5 Ultra: Everything you need to know
content:
Macworld






New Mac Studio 2026: At a glance
What’s new: The 2026 Mac Studio gains M5 Max and M5 Ultra chips, dramatically faster AI and graphics performance, faster SSD storage, increased memory bandwidth, Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and enhanced professional connectivity. 
Release date: Announced on August 25, 2026
Price: From $2,499/£2,499
Pre-orders: Pre-order now
On sale: Shipping starts on September 22, 2026  but the Mac Studio with 512GB of unified memory is coming in late October.
Apple has launched a new Mac Studio to replace the M4 Max and M3 Ultra model introduced 17 months ago, in March 2025. Externally, the 2026 Mac Studio retains what Apple calls its “signature compact design,” with the most significant upgrades taking place inside.
The previous generation was unusual because it mixed chip generations, pairing M4 Max with M3 Ultra. The 2026 models bring both tiers into the M5 family, with M5 Max and the new M5 Ultra. M5 Max offers an 18-core CPU and up to a 40-core GPU, while M5 Ultra scales to a 36-core CPU and 80-core GPU. Neural Accelerators are now built into every GPU core to boost AI performance.
Apple claims up to 1.3x faster CPU performance, 1.8x faster graphics and 4.3x faster AI performance, depending on the configuration and workload. M5 Max also adds third-generation hardware-accelerated ray tracing, while M5 Ultra can play up to 33 streams of 8K ProRes 422 video simultaneously. Elsewhere, PCIe Gen 6-based SSDs deliver up to twice the storage performance, while Apple’s N1 chip adds Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6. USB-C genlock, support for up to eight displays, and Thunderbolt 5 clustering for distributed AI workloads are also new.


When is the new Mac Studio available?
The new Mac Studio with M5 Max and M5 Ultra was announced on August 25, 2026, but it won’t start shipping until September 22. Even then, not every configuration will be available: Apple says Mac Studio models configured with 512GB of unified memory won’t arrive until “late October.”
You can pre-order the new Mac Studio now, though, and if you want one we’d recommend ordering early. Ongoing chip and component shortages have constrained Mac availability, so some configurations may face constrained availability, particularly high-memory models.

Has the Mac Studio price gone up?
In June 2026, Apple raised the starting price of the Mac Studio by $500, from $1,999 to $2,499. The M3 Ultra model saw an even steeper increase, rising $1,300 from its $3,999 launch price to $5,299. The hikes were part of broader increases across the Mac lineup, which Apple attributed to sharply higher component costs, particularly RAM.
The new M5 Max Mac Studio remains at the June price of $2,499, but the M5 Ultra model has risen by another $200 to $5,499. That makes it $1,500 more expensive than the previous-generation Ultra model was when it launched in March 2025.
Here’s a breakdown of the key price changes for the Mac Studio:

When it comes to high prices, the M5 Ultra Mac Studio is filling the gap left by the the removal of the Mac Pro from the line up back in March 2026.

Mac Studio M5 Max and M5 Ultra specs

				
					

				
			
Petter Ahrnstedt




Mac Studio moves to M5 Max and M5 Ultra, with up to a 36-core CPU, 80-core GPU, 512GB unified memory and 1.2TB/s memory bandwidth. Storage now uses PCIe Gen 6 for twice the performance, while connectivity adds Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and USB-C genlock. 
Processor: M5 Ultra and M5 Max chip compared
The Mac Studio comes with either Apple’s Max or Ultra chips. The Max chip is aimed at demanding professional and creative workflows and supports large amounts of unified memory and high memory bandwidth. The Max chip is also available as an option for the MacBook Pro. 
The Ultra chip combines two Max chips on one large chip using Apple’s UltraFusion architecture, so they offer double the CPU and GPU resources, and even higher memory capacity and bandwidth. It’s suited to complex 3D rendering, large AI models and scientific computing. 
M5 Max: We are already familiar with the M5 Max from the MacBook Pro that launched in March 2026. It offers an 18-core CPU and up to 40-core GPU, versus up to 16 CPU cores in the M4 Max. Its GPU includes a Neural Accelerator in every core, helping deliver up to 3.9x faster AI performance than M4 Max, according to Apple, alongside third-generation ray tracing. 
M5 Ultra: The M5 Ultra is a brand new chip that combines two M5 Max dies and offers up to a 36-core CPU and 80-core GPU. Apple claims up to 1.3x faster CPU, 1.8x faster graphics and 4.3x AI compute versus M3 Ultra.


						

							


Storage 
Maximum storage remains 16TB, so capacity hasn’t increased. 
The storage should be much faster though. Apple has introduced a next-generation SSD architecture based on PCIe Gen 6, which it claims delivers up to twice the storage performance. That should mean faster project loading, file transfers and loading of very large local AI models


						

							


RAM
Maximum unified memory remains 128GB with M5 Max and 512GB with M5 Ultra, the same as the previous generation. 
Bandwidth has improved though. The M5 Max will now reach 614GB/s, up from 546GB/s on the top M4 Max, while M5 Ultra delivers 1.2TB/s, which Apple says is around 50 percent higher than M3 Ultra.


						

							


Connectivity: WiFi & Bluetooth

				
					

				
			
Eugen Wegmann




Wi-Fi: The Mac Studio now supports Wi-Fi 7 which replaces the previous wireless standard Wi-Fi 6E.
Bluetooth: Bluetooth 6 replaces Bluetooth 5.3.
Ethernet: Existing connectivity including 10Gb Ethernet, HDMI, USB-A, SDXC and a headphone jack remains.




Thunderbolt: Thunderbolt 5 remains, offering up to 120Gb/s and as many as six Thunderbolt 5 ports depending on configuration. Thunderbolt 5 can now be used with RDMA to cluster multiple Mac Studios for distributed AI workloads; Apple says four systems can deliver up to 3x faster AI inference than one. 
Genlock: Apple has added Genlock support over USB-C. This is used for synchronising a display and camera (which can be an iPhone 17 Pro) and will be useful for professional video workflows.
Display support: The Mac Studio will support up to eight displays, including up to four Studio Display XDR displays at 5K/120Hz.
Other ports include two USB-C ports and an SDXC card slot on the front of the M5 Max model, and two Thunderbolt 5 ports and an SDXC card slot on the front of the M5 Ultra model. On the back of the Mac Studio are:
4× Thunderbolt 5 ports
2× USB-A ports
1× HDMI port
1× 10Gb Ethernet port
1× 3.5mm headphone jack

Who is the Mac Studio best for?
Apple has designed the Mac Studio with M5 Max to meet the needs of demanding creative and technical professionals. Apple specifically highlights musicians, photographers, software developers, designers and 3D professionals. It’s also well suited to video editing, code compilation, AI image generation and running sizeable LLMs locally.
The Mac Studio with M5 Ultra is intended for professionals with exceptionally demanding workloads: VFX artists rendering complex scenes, filmmakers working with multiple streams of 8K video, engineers running simulations, and AI researchers or data scientists training and running huge models locally. Its 512GB memory ceiling is particularly valuable for frontier-class LLMs.


						

							


Should you buy the 2026 Mac Studio?
Availability is likely to be limited due to the global RAM shortages so we expect that stock will quickly run out.

title: Apple Magic Keyboards get cosmetic updates, avoid price hikes
content:
Macworld





If you’re planning on investing in a new M6 Mac mini or M5 Ultra Mac Studio, you might be buying a new Apple Magic Keyboard along with it. Apple has updated its keyboards, too: Certain keys have had their labels changed to symbols instead of names.
Apple introduced these changes with the MacBook Neo and M5 MacBook Air, so the company is basically catching up on normalizing the keys. The Tab, Caps Lock, Shift, Delete, and Return keys no longer have their respective word labels. Instead, they have arrow icons:
Tab is now ⇥
Caps Lock is now ⇪
Shift is now ⇧
Delete is now ⌫
Return looks similar to ↵ (see photo above)
The switch to the graphical labeling is an effort to standardize its keyboards. Apple’s non-English keyboards have used symbols, and implementing them in the English keyboard streamlines the production process. However, Apple did not update the keys on the $129 wireless Magic Keyboard with Numeric Keypad that has a Lightning connection for charging.
Speaking of the production process, it appears that the Magic Keyboards have not been affected by the worldwide RAM shortage (/sarcasm), so their prices have not changed:

title: New Mac mini M6 and M5 Pro: Everything you need to know
content:
Macworld






New Mac mini 2026: At a glance
What’s new: The 2026 Mac mini delivers much faster performance, especially for graphics and AI, thanks to the M6 and M5 Pro chips. It also brings faster storage and upgraded connectivity, with Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and 2.5Gb Ethernet as standard.
Release date: Announced on August 25, 2026
Price: From $899/£899
Pre-orders: Pre-order now
On sale: September 22, 2026
Apple has launched a new Mac mini to replace the M4 and M4 Pro Mac mini which was introduced in October 2024. Externally the 2026 Mac mini looks just as it did following the redesign in October 2024 – it’s still a five-by-five-inch square with two front USB-C ports and the headphone jack, with three Thunderbolt ports, HDMI and Ethernet on the rear. It’s what’s inside that has changed.
The new Mac mini models offer new chips, the M6 and the M5 Pro. This is a similar scenario to a few years ago when Apple launched the M4 Mac Studio alongside the M3 Ultra Mac Studio. There is likely to be some confusion about the chip generations so we will explain the differences in more detail below.
These new chips offer a significant jump in performance, especially relating to AI. With this update it is particularly apparent that Apple is positioning the Mac mini as an AI machine.


When is the new Mac mini available?
The new Mac mini M6 and M5 Pro models were announced on August 25, 2026, but they won’t actually ship until September 22.
You can pre-order now though, and if you want one we recommend doing so because the chip shortages that have plagued the industry are likely to mean stock quickly runs out.

We had hoped this meant Mac mini pricing would remain at the June level for the foreseeable future. Unfortunately, with the arrival of the new models, Apple has raised prices again—this time by a further $100/£100.

Mac mini M6 and M5 Pro specs
As well as the move from M4 and M4 Pro to M6 and M5 Pro, the Mac mini also gains storage that is up to twice as fast, according to Apple, Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, 2.5Gb Ethernet and USB-C genlock support. 

				
					

				
			
The new M6 chip has launched in the Mac mini. 

Apple




Processor: M6 and M5 Pro chip compared
There may be some confusion over the chip generations in the new Mac mini. The mainstream model uses the newer M6 chip, while the more powerful model uses the older-generation M5 Pro. Pro chips are designed for heavier professional workloads, with more CPU and GPU cores, higher memory bandwidth, support for more unified memory, additional displays and faster Thunderbolt connectivity. So while M5 Pro remains the more capable chip overall, the M6 offers a significant step up from the M4 it replaces in the previous generation Mac mini. We will be running benchmarks on the M6 in comparison to the M5 as soon as we can get our hands on one. 
M6: The Mac mini is the first Mac to ship with the M6 chip, replacing the M4 in the entry-level model. It features a 12-core CPU and 12-core GPU, up from 10 CPU and GPU cores in the previous generation, and supports up 170GB/s memory bandwidth if you choose 24GB or 32GB memory (the 16GB configuration offers 153GB/s bandwidth). Apple promises up to 40% faster CPU performance, twice the graphics performance and up to 4x faster AI performance than M4. It also introduces Apple’s first Dual 16-core Neural Engine, delivering up to twice the Neural Engine performance.
M5 Pro: The M5 Pro replaces the M4 Pro in the higher-end Mac mini and can be configured with up to an 18-core CPU and 20-core GPU. Apple claims up to 4x faster LLM processing, 1.4x faster Blender ray-tracing performance and 1.5x faster Affinity image processing than M4 Pro. It supports up to 64GB of unified memory with 307GB/s memory bandwidth. Both chips feature Neural Accelerators in their GPU cores, but the M5 Pro’s additional CPU and GPU cores, greater memory capacity and higher bandwidth make it better suited to video production, 3D rendering, development and larger local AI models.
With both of these chips the focus is very much on AI with Apple emphasising that both the M6 and M5 Pro incorporate Neural Accelerators in their GPU cores. 


						

							


Storage 
Apple claims the new M6 Mac mini offers up to 2x faster storage compared to the previous generation.
Other than that the storage capacities are as before – 256GB,  512GB, 1TB and 2TB for the M6 model and 512GB, 1TB, 2TB, 4TB and 8TB SSDs for the M5 Pro model. 


						

							


RAM
The new M6 model supports 32GB RAM unlike the M4 model which maxed out at 24GB. 
The new M5 Pro model supports a maximum of 64GB RAM, up from 48GB.


						

							


Connectivity: WiFi & Bluetooth

				
					

				
			
Simon Jary / Foundry




Wi-Fi: Both models now support Wi-Fi 7 which replaces the previous wireless standard Wi-Fi 6E.
Bluetooth: Both models also move to Bluetooth 6, replacing Bluetooth 5.3.
Ethernet: Previously faster Ethernet was an upgrade; the new models now have 2.5Gb Ethernet, with 10Gb Ethernet available as a configurable option.
Thunderbolt: The M6 Mac mini has three Thunderbolt 4 ports and the the M5 Pro version has three Thunderbolt 5 ports. This is the same as the previous generation.
Genlock: Apple has added Genlock support over USB-C. This is used for synchronising a display and camera (which can be an iPhone 17 Pro). It is aimed at professional video workflows
Display support: The M6 Mac mini will support up to two 6K displays plus one 5K display, while the M5 Pro supports up to three 6K displays. 
Other ports include two USB-C/USB 3 ports and a headphone jack on the front and HDMI and Ethernet remain on the rear, as previously.

title: Amid raging price hikes, Apple slashes flagship cloth by more than 50%
content:
Macworld





On a day of high-priced product announcements, Apple has offered a crumb of comfort to its more cash-strapped customers: the beloved Polishing Cloth has dropped in price by a whopping 53 percent. Relentlessly memed on for charging a faintly absurd $19 for the square cloth at launch three years ago, the company is now happy to accept just $9 for seemingly the same product.
The common thread uniting Tuesday’s two big Mac updates was prices going up. The M6 Mac mini starts at $899, up from $599 for the equivalent M4 model just two months ago. The M5 Ultra Mac Studio, meanwhile, starts at $5,499, a price hike of another $200 over the previous price hike. But the Polishing Cloth went against the grain with a huge price drop.
Apple didn’t send out a press release advertising the nonabrasive fabric accessory’s new bargain price. Instead, it quietly removed the previous store entry (which carried the product code MW693AM/A) and put up a new one in its place (MLH74AM/A) with an updated price. Other than the price and code, it appears to be an identical product with an identical description.
As before, that includes the endlessly amusing Compatibility section, which lists every iPhone and iPad going back to 2012, every single Apple Watch, and a huge list of MacBooks. In some ways, it’s surprising the company bothered to make the list since the description makes it clear that the Polishing Cloth cleans any Apple display, but we appreciate the effort.
Whether this bargain price will last remains to be seen. Unlike other Apple devices the Polishing Cloth is unlikely to be affected by the ongoing memory shortage, but we’ll be monitoring international microfiber shipments with the greatest of interest.

While all eyes are on the upcoming iPhone event, Apple threw us a curveball Tuesday morning with a rare August launch of an updated Mac Studio with the all-new M5 Ultra processor.
The new Mac Studio is visually identical to the previous model but has major upgrades inside. Instead of the M4 Max and M3 Ultra, you can now buy a Mac Studio with an M5 Max or M5 Ultra processor, with up to a whopping 512GB of RAM. Here are the specs Apple is offering for the two chips:

While the M5 Ultra is still double the capability of the M5 Max, Apple touts its “next-generation UltraFusion technology to form a quad-die architecture for the first time in an M-series chip.” The previous UltraFusion interconnector linked two Max dies over 10,000 high-speed connections that offer low latency and high bandwidth. It was previously reported that Apple was working to create a new version of the Ultra chip with more advanced UltraFusion architecture.
Apple is leaning hard into AI and calls the M5 Ultra Mac Studio “a game changer for AI workloads” and says “AI coding agents process significantly faster, image generation tools can render creations in an instant, and enterprise teams can cluster multiple systems to scale performance to new heights.” 
In addition to the new chips, the Mac Studio now has an N1 chip to bring Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, as well as “a next-generation SSD architecture built on PCIe Gen 6.” We already praised the MacBook Pro for its super-fast storage speeds, and Apple now claims the new SSDs deliver “industry-leading read and write speeds for rapid project loading, file transfers, and loading huge LLMs.”
Now for the not-so-good news. While the M5 Max model starts at the same $2,499 as the post-price-hike M4 Max, the M5 Ultra Mac Studio now starts at $5,499, an increase of another $200 over the previous price hike. That means you’re paying $1,500 more than if you bought an M3 Ultra Mac Studio before June. You’re also paying more for storage and RAM, so get ready to shell out well over 20 grand for a fully loaded model (which won’t be available until October). The most expensive M5 Ultra you can get now, with 256GB of RAM and 16TB of storage, costs $18,299.
The M5 Mac Studio is available for pre-order now but won’t begin shipping until September 22.

title: Apple launches new M6 Mac mini with another price hike
content:
Macworld





As predicted on this site earlier today, Apple has announced the launch of a new Mac mini model with M5 and M6 chip options. It doesn’t feature any design changes or external upgrades, but it does offer a two-generation bump in processors compared to the previous model.
Slightly confusingly, the version of the Mac mini with a chip from the M5 generation is the more powerful of the two, because it’s the M5 Pro. This spec starts at $1,699 for a 15-core CPU and 16-core GPU, but customers have the option to bump that to 18 and 20 cores, respectively, for an additional $200. There are also configuration options to increase RAM from the starting 24GB or storage from the baseline 512GB, and to upgrade to 10 Gigabit Ethernet. The RAM options remain the same, but the 64GB highest-end option now costs $1,000.
More appealing for the Mac mini’s traditional budget market will be the M6 model, which starts at a far more manageable $899. That, however, is still a $100 increase over the M4 model from 2024 that it replaces. Worse, the M4 model started at just $599 until June, when Apple responded to the ongoing memory crunch by imposing brutal price hikes. In other words, the cheapest entry point to Apple’s desktop Mac ecosystem has jumped by $300, or 50 percent, in the space of two months.
The $899 version isn’t exactly a state-of-the-art build, either. The entry-level configuration comes with 16GB of RAM and just 256GB of storage. We should note that it is possible to get this spec for $799, but only if you’re an education buyer. Of note, the Mac mini is not available for the Apple Upgrade program either.

				
					

				
			
Apple




The price hike is likely to weaken the Mac mini’s appeal among budget buyers, but (aside from the necessity to accommodate increasing component costs) Apple may not care. In his report predicting that a new mini was on the way, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman noted that the machine had become increasingly popular for running AI applications locally, and that Apple was struggling to meet demand. The company may not mind if fewer customers are prepared to pay the asking price, since there are plenty of AI fans ready to take their place.
Those AI fans will likely be tempted by a new model with a new chip. Apple boasts that the M6 delivers “gains across every dimension of performance” and “the ideal balance of performance, power efficiency, and on-device AI to effortlessly fly through daily tasks, coding, and creative projects.”
In numerical terms, the company claims the M6 version of the Mac will deliver up to 4x faster AI performance, 2x faster storage and graphics, and 40% faster CPU performance than the M4 mini. The M5 Pro model, meanwhile, is rated by its maker as up to 8.5x faster at LLM prompt processing than its M2 Pro predecessor, and up to 4x faster than the M4 Pro model. Naturally we will put those claims to the test in our labs.
Another surprise is how early Apple has announced the new Mac mini. Pre-orders are open now, but it won’t go on sale until 22 September, almost a month from now.
This is no longer a budget Mac.

The machine also gains Thunderbolt 5 ports with up to 120Gb/s of bandwidth, along with Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 for the first time via Apple's N1 chip. The new ‌Mac Studio‌ also supports genlock over USB-C and can drive up to eight displays.

The M5 Ultra chip includes an up to 36-core CPU that contains 12 super cores and 24 performance cores. It delivers up to 1.25x higher single-threaded performance and up to 1.3x higher multithreaded performance than the M3 Ultra from the previous generation ‌Mac Studio‌. 

M1 Ultra. Apple says the GPU's latest shader core technology, paired with second-generation Dynamic Caching, hardware-accelerated mesh shading, and third-generation ray tracing, delivers up to 40% faster graphics performance than the M3 Ultra. 

The chip also includes a more capable Media Engine, with dedicated hardware for H.264, HEVC, four ProRes encode and decode engines, and hardware-accelerated AV1 decode, along with a 32-core Neural Engine for on-device AI tasks.




The M5 Ultra is built by connecting two dual-die M5 Max chips using Apple's next-generation UltraFusion technology, which increases inter-die bandwidth to over 4.4TB/s and connection density by more than 6x, allowing the four dies to function as a single processor.

The new ‌Mac Studio‌ with the M5 Ultra supports up to 512GB of unified memory and up to 1.2TB/s of memory bandwidth, which is a 50% increase over M3 Ultra. Apple says the added memory and bandwidth allows users to store large datasets locally, increase tokens per second, and run large language models with hundreds of billions of parameters entirely on device.

Users can also cluster multiple ‌Mac Studio‌ systems together using built-in support for Thunderbolt 5 and RDMA (remote direct memory access), creating a shared memory pool across systems. Apple says a cluster of four ‌Mac Studio‌ systems delivers up to 3x faster AI inference than a single system.

The ‌Mac Studio‌ is also now available with the M5 Max chip, offering an 18-core CPU with 6 super cores and 12 performance cores, up to 40 GPU cores, up to 128GB of unified memory with up to 614GB/s of memory bandwidth, and up to 8TB of storage. Apple says the M5 Max delivers up to 3.9x faster AI performance than the previous generation.

UltraFusion increases inter-die bandwidth to over 4.4TB/s and connection density by more than 6x, allowing the four dies to function as a single processor.

The chip includes an CPU with up to 36 cores, containing 12 super cores and 24 performance cores, delivering up to 1.25x higher single-threaded performance and up to 1.3x higher multithreaded performance than the M3 Ultra.

Its GPU scales up to 80 cores, with a Neural Accelerator built into each core for the first time on an Ultra chip. Apple says this delivers up to 4.3x the peak AI compute performance compared to the M3 Ultra, along with up to 1.8x faster graphics than the previous-generation chip.
